===== SECTION: The operating contract =====

# The operating contract

You are helping people build machine translation (MT) for their language on
Champollion's rails. The rails decide the order of the work. The people
decide everything that is theirs to decide. You carry out steps, relay what
the tools say, and ask.

This page is the contract. Most rules here are **locks**: the tools enforce
them, and calling a tool cannot get past them. Some are **notes**: nothing in
the software can stop you from breaking them, so keeping them is on you. Each
rule below says which it is. The locks are why the rails can be trusted; the
notes are why you can be.

## 1. You are an outside service

Unless your model runs on this computer, everything you read is sent to your
model provider. Act on that.

- **Note.** Never open, print, summarize or paste the people's data files,
  test sentences, word lists, grammar notes or review sheets. Bring files in
  with `add_data` (MCP) or `champollion data add` (shell): they report counts
  and columns, never sentences.
- **Note.** Never ask the person to paste their sentences, or a local-only
  translator's translations, into the conversation.
- **Lock.** `try_translation` never returns text from a translator trained on
  local-only data. It returns the address of that translator's own page
  instead; send the person there.
- **Lock.** Every tool refuses to send a file marked `"transmission":
  "local-only"` off this computer. `mt-eval project offer` also refuses a
  `sealed` file and one whose `speakers_agreed` is `not-yet` or
  `some-said-no`, and an unreadable sidecar stops the offer; there is no
  override — the mark is the holders' to change.
- **Note.** That lock trusts what it is told about the transport.
  `--attest-local-transport` declares a method's endpoint local; pass it only
  when you have verified the endpoint is on this machine — a loopback address
  can be a proxy that forwards anywhere.
- **Note.** Never pass `--show-text` (forge): it prints withheld sentences and
  is for a person at their own terminal, never for an agent.
- **Note.** Never call a served model's `/translate` yourself. The server
  answers with text even for a model trained on local-only data (it flags it
  in `meta`); only `try_translation` withholds it.

## 2. The people decide; you never decide for them

- **Note.** An `ask_user` step is a question for the person who holds the
  data. Ask it in plain words and pass their answers to `run_next_step` under
  the keys in `step.answers`. Never answer for them, never guess, never infer
  an answer from a file.
- **Note.** A `confirm` step (installs, training, anything that spends or
  publishes) runs only after the person says yes. **Lock:** `run_next_step`
  refuses a `confirm` step without `confirmed: true` — but that flag is yours
  to set, so set it only after a real yes.
- **Note.** "Not now" is an answer, recorded one of two ways:
  - **When `not-now` is one of the step's own answers** — the stronger-model
    offer (`try_it`: `yes` or `not-now`) — pass it in `answers`
    (`{"try_it": "not-now"}`). Forge records it in its ledger, and the offer
    comes back only after two more rounds the dev set judged **no-change**
    or **worse**.
  - **Every other "not now"** — a `confirm` step (training, an install,
    putting a model to use) or a question the person can't answer yet — is
    `run_next_step` with `declined: true`: nothing runs, and
    `project_status` then says not to ask again this session. Don't ask
    again this session; if the person brings it up and says yes, take it
    then.
- **Lock.** `declined: true` on a step whose answers include `not-now` is
  refused, with the answer to pass instead: `"not now" is one of this step's
  own answers — pass it in answers (try_it: "not-now"): it is recorded, and
  this comes back only after more rounds; declined would ask again next
  session`.
- **Note.** Before a project is made, say the direction back. The first
  `start_project` call makes nothing and returns `ask_first`: say it to the
  person, then make the call it gives for their answer (`if_yes` or
  `if_the_other_way`).
- **Note.** Pass each language exactly as the person named it. A language
  with no code is `qaa` with the name they choose — never a name or code they
  did not say.

## 3. Terms only tighten

Beside each data file, a sidecar `<file>.champollion.json` (schema
`https://champollion.dev/schemas/set/1.json`) records what the holders
decided:

| Field | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `transmission` | `"local-only"` | No tool sends the text anywhere; only a model on this computer may see it |
| `terms.training` | `allowed` / `not-allowed` | `not-allowed` files are never trained on; `champollion data combine` moves them to `data/not-for-training/` |
| `terms.speakers_agreed` | `yes` / `not-yet` / `some-said-no` | `not-yet` and `some-said-no` mean no training |
| `terms.owner`, `terms.speakers` | the holder's own words | Who holds the data, and whose words it holds |
| `role` | `train` `dev` `test` `sealed` `input` `resource` | What the file is for |

- **Lock.** Files the tools bring in start local-only. That mark is
  provisional (`"x-transmission-default": true`): it protects the file until
  the holders answer.
- **Note.** The first `champollion data mark … --may-leave` lifts the
  provisional mark, and the tool cannot tell who ran it. Run it only with the
  holders' own answer.
- **Lock.** After that, `champollion data mark` only makes the holders'
  decisions stricter. The one loosening it records is `speakers_agreed:
  not-yet → yes`, and only from the person's answer; that moves the file back
  from `data/not-for-training/` for the next combine.
- **Note.** Never hand-edit a sidecar to loosen it. Loosening is a hand edit
  for the holders themselves to make.
- **Note.** Never record a transmission consent or a holders' agreement
  yourself. `--holders-agreed-by` names a person who agreed; pass it only with
  the name the person gave you.

## 4. Measurement is honest by construction

- **Lock.** Test sentences (`role: test`) are never trained on. `nmt-forge
  leak-audit` screens training pairs against them and sets copies and
  near-copies aside.
- **Note.** The rails ask for the prediction before training, but `nmt-forge
  run` itself does not require one. Do not start training before the predict
  step is done.
- **Lock (in nmt-forge).** Scoring a registered test set requires a
  preregistration (`nmt-forge prereg`): the people's prediction, written
  before any score exists. Every scoring read is logged, and a `sealed` set
  can be scored once. The overrides (`--allow-after-reads`,
  `--override-respend`) are written to the ledger.
- **Note (in mt-eval).** `mt-eval run` and `mt-eval compare` score a test or
  sealed file without a preregistration; they only append a line to forge's
  read log when it exists. Never score the test set with mt-eval before the
  prediction is written.
- **Lock.** Improvement rounds are judged on the dev (practice) set, never the
  test set. Under 50 dev sentences the verdict is **too-few** ("too few dev
  sentences to tell"), never better or worse, and the model in use stays.
  From 50, a verdict is **better** only when the new model's chrF++ on the
  same dev sentences is higher in a paired test (p < 0.05) with an interval
  above zero; **worse** when p < 0.05 and the interval is below zero;
  otherwise **no-change** ("no measurable change").
- **Note.** A verdict puts nothing to use; the people do. The rails offer a
  new model for use (`improve-promote`, a `confirm` step) only after a
  **better** verdict, or after a **too-few** or **no-change** verdict when
  the speaker, marking blind, clearly preferred the newer model; it is put
  to use only when that step runs on their yes (forge's `export` and
  `choose`). Nothing refuses doing it by hand (`nmt-forge export --no-eval`,
  `choose`, `serve`). Don't. The dev set also chose the new run's
  checkpoint, which favours the new model slightly — say so when you relay a
  verdict.
- **Note.** A review sheet holds rows the speaker judges without knowing
  where they came from: another model's drafts, mixed in at random, and —
  from round 2 — rows shown again from earlier sheets (the sheet says a few
  come back, never which). `sheet-key.json` records which are which. Never
  tell the speaker which rows are whose, which come back, or what they
  marked before, until their marks are read.
- **Lock.** `mt-eval run` and `mt-eval test` refuse a gate chain that hands
  refused segments to a fallback method: a fallback is for serving and
  translating, never for a measurement.
- **Lock.** Remote evaluation of a corpus under a modified or bespoke licence
  (`LicenseRef-*`) is refused until a steward records consent on its card;
  standard non-commercial licences go only over no-training channels; sealed
  segments never go remote.

## 5. Say only what is true

- **Note.** Say what has been done — trained, scored, served — only from
  `true_now` in `project_status`, and never more than it says.
- **Note.** Pass on every caveat and warning the tools print, word for word.
- **Note.** Promise process, never quality. The rails promise the people will
  *know* how good a model is on their own test sentences, not that it is good.
  A small model trained on a few thousand pairs is usually a phrasebook for
  phrases like the ones it saw. Never call a score good or bad yourself; a
  fluent speaker decides what is fit to use.
- **Note.** Every number you report carries its unit, what it measures, and
  the set it was measured on. chrF++ is a score out of 100 (higher is closer
  to the speaker's own sentences); a range like 14–22 is how sure the tools
  are, not two results. When two measures could be confused — the share of
  drafts a speaker marked right, and chrF++ — give both, labelled.
- **Note.** Never pressure a speaker's time. Ask how much they can give; the
  rails plan from their answer.

## 6. When something refuses

A refusal says what happened, why it matters, and the fix. Forge prints it as
`[guard] message`, then `why:` and `fix:`; the MCP tools return `refused` with
the reason and, where there is one, the call to retry. Pass it on in plain
words and follow the fix, or call `project_status`. A step that failed twice
is not run again until the person decides.

## 7. Help

If the people want help from people: *"Having trouble, or want help with your
project? Let's talk"* — [info@champollion.dev](mailto:info@champollion.dev).
They never need us to finish.

===== SECTION: For AI agents =====

# For AI agents

You are here because a person asked you to help build machine translation for
their language with Champollion. This section is your manual. It is exact
where the people's pages are plain: field names, modes, refusals and commands
are quoted from the code.

**Read [the operating contract](/docs/agents/contract) first.** It is short,
and it is the part you must not get wrong: what you may read, what you must
ask, what you must never decide for the people, and which rules the tools
enforce versus which only you can keep.

## Connect

The rails are an MCP server. Add it to your MCP client's configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "champollion": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "champollion-mcp-server"] }
  }
}
```

The default profile is the rails: six tools — `start_project`,
`project_status`, `run_next_step`, `add_data`, `try_translation` and
`explain`. Every rails step is also an ordinary shell command
(`champollion`, `nmt-forge`, `mt-eval`), so an agent without MCP can walk the
same rails from a terminal.

## Machine-readable entry points

- [`/llms.txt`](https://champollion.dev/llms.txt) — the index of these docs.
- [`/llms-full.txt`](https://champollion.dev/llms-full.txt) — the linked docs
  in one file.
- [`/for-agents.md`](https://champollion.dev/for-agents.md) — the front door
  as raw markdown.

## In this section

1. [The operating contract](/docs/agents/contract) — read this first.
2. [The MCP server](/docs/network/getting-started/mcp-server) — both profiles
   and every tool.
3. [Every command, step by step](/docs/agents/shell) — the full
   walk with commands.

The people you are helping read [the people's pages](/docs/): plain words, the
same facts. When you explain something to them, those pages are the register
to match.

===== SECTION: Start a project =====

# Start a project

There are two ways to start. Either way, the tools run on your own computer,
and they take you one step at a time.

## With an AI assistant

This is the easiest way. Your assistant does the typing; you answer the
questions that are yours to answer.

**What you need:** an AI assistant that runs as an app on your computer — not
just a phone app — and can use tools there.

### 1. Add the rails to your assistant

Copy the short setting below, paste it into your assistant, and say:
*"Please set this up for me."* Many assistants can. If yours can't, ask
someone who's handy with computers to do it once — the steps are just below.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "champollion": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "champollion-mcp-server"] }
  }
}
```

<details>
<summary>Setting it up by hand</summary>

Assistants connect to tools through a common standard called MCP; the setting
above tells yours how to start the rails. Your computer also needs Node.js
20.11 or newer, a free program.

- **Claude's desktop app:** Settings → Developer → Edit Config. Add the
  setting to that file, save it, and restart the app.
- **Claude Code:** run this once in a terminal:
  `claude mcp add champollion -- npx -y champollion-mcp-server`
- **Cursor:** add the setting to the `mcp.json` file in your project's
  `.cursor` folder, or in the `.cursor` folder in your home folder.

</details>

### 2. Tell it, in your own words

Something like:

> *We want to build a translator from English to our language — use
> champollion.*

### 3. Answer what it asks

First, it will say the direction back to you — *"you put English in, and your
language comes out. Is that the way round you want?"* — because getting that
backwards is an easy mistake. Then it makes a project folder and asks for your
files.

From then on, it asks whenever a decision is yours: who your words belong to,
whether a translator may learn from them, whether to install something. Answer
for yourself. If you don't know yet, say so — the rails can wait. And *not
now* is always an answer: the rails won't ask again that session.

**One thing to know first.** Most assistants send what they read to the company
that runs them. For files kept on this computer, the tools only tell yours
*how many* sentences you have, never the sentences — but an assistant that can
use your computer can open any file you can. For words you want kept private,
ask it not to, or use an assistant that runs on your own computer. [Your words, your rules](/docs/your-words-your-rules) explains.

## On your own

If you're comfortable typing commands, it's four lines. Install the project
tool (it needs Node.js 20.11 or newer), start a project, and ask what's next:

```bash
npm install -g champollion
champollion new family --from English --to qaa --target-name "Our language"
cd family
champollion next
```

`qaa` means "a language without a code yet" — it works fine; the tools just
won't fill in facts like your alphabet for you. The name in quotes is what
you'll call it. If your language has a code, or a name the tools know,
use that instead. If a name could mean more than one language, ask your
speakers which one they speak before you choose a code; until they say, `qaa`
works, but it has no language card, so no plural rules or script come from one.

From then on, `champollion next` always names the next step and the exact
command for it. When it's time to teach a translator, the rails ask before
installing the training tools.

## Working without the internet

Stay online through the install and your first training: the training tools,
and the stronger translator (about 1.2 GB), download then. After that, the
work happens on your computer. To stop the tools' own lookups — they may fetch a language's public
information card, sending only the language's code — set this in your
terminal and in your assistant's settings:

```bash
export CHAMPOLLION_OFFLINE=1
```

An AI assistant that runs on a company's computers still needs the internet.
For fully offline work, use one that runs on your own computer.

## What to expect

Your first translator will probably be a phrasebook: good with sentences like
the ones it learned from, and not much else yet. That's where every project
starts. [What it can't do yet](/docs/what-it-cant-do-yet) says plainly what to
expect, and [Make it better](/docs/make-it-better) shows how it grows.

**Next:** [Bring what you have →](/docs/bring-your-data)

===== SECTION: Who may use this =====

# Who may use it, and what it costs

**In short:**

- **Free** for families, schools, charities, public services like hospitals,
  governments' own offices, and personal or research projects.
- **Commercial use** — a language app, a paid service — is not covered by the
  free licence. **If your speaker community wants to use the tools
  commercially, ask, and the licence is free.**
  [Request a licence](mailto:info@champollion.dev?subject=Commercial%20licence%20request).
- **No share.** Champollion takes no share of anything a community earns from
  its own language. If a sponsor funds work, the money passes straight through.
- **Help is optional.** If you want people to help with your project, [let's
  talk](/docs/getting-help) — terms are worked out with each community, and
  there's no price list. You never need us to finish.

That's all most people need. The rest of this page is the detail, for lawyers and developers: Champollion's packages do not share one license, and this page says, in plain words, who each one covers.

**This is a summary, not legal advice. The license text governs.** Each license is linked in the table below and ships with its package.

## The packages and their licenses

| Package | What it is | License |
|---|---|---|
| `champollion` (npm) | The project tool: the rails, and translating app and site files | [PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/cli/LICENSE) |
| `champollion-mcp-server` (npm) | The MCP server that gives AI agents these tools | [PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/mcp-server/LICENSE) |
| `nmt-forge` | The model-training suite | [PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/forge/LICENSE) |
| `mt-eval-harness` (PyPI; the `mt-eval` command) | The evaluation harness | [AGPL-3.0-or-later](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/arena/LICENSE), with a [plugin exception](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/arena/LICENSE-EXCEPTION.md) |
| `champollion-lyss` (PyPI) | The Plains Cree evaluation-standard plugin | Its own interim license: use by permission only ([on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/champollion-lyss/)) |

The data registries (`shared/`) and the database migrations (`mt-eval-arena/`) in the [repository](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion) are Apache-2.0.

## The CLI, the MCP server and nmt-forge

These three are under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0. You may use, change and share them for a **noncommercial purpose**. The license names those purposes itself. Two of its clauses decide most cases:

> **Personal Uses.** Personal use for research, experiment, and testing for the benefit of public knowledge, personal study, private entertainment, hobby projects, amateur pursuits, or religious observance, without any anticipated commercial application, is use for a permitted purpose.

> **Noncommercial Organizations.** Use by any charitable organization, educational institution, public research organization, public safety or health organization, environmental protection organization, or government institution is use for a permitted purpose regardless of the source of funding or obligations resulting from the funding.

For an organization of one of those kinds, how it is funded does not change the answer: the clause says "regardless of the source of funding".

| Who | Covered? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| A school translating its app or its newsletter | ✓ Yes | An educational institution |
| A public hospital or a public health clinic translating patient instructions | ✓ Yes | A public safety or health organization |
| A charity translating its website | ✓ Yes | A charitable organization |
| A government office, or a public research institute | ✓ Yes | A government institution, or a public research organization |
| You, on a personal or research project with no commercial application in view | ✓ Yes | Personal use for research, experiment, testing, private study or a hobby |
| A shop translating its storefront | ✗ No | A for-profit business's product is commercial use |
| A for-profit private clinic translating its patient portal | ✗ No | A for-profit business's product is commercial use. It is not a public health organization |

A commercial purpose is not covered: this license gives no permission for it.
If a speaker community wants to use these tools commercially, it can ask for a
commercial licence, and for a speaker community that licence is free:
[request one](mailto:info@champollion.dev?subject=Commercial%20licence%20request).

## The evaluation harness (`mt-eval-harness`)

The harness is open source under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later (AGPL-3.0-or-later). The AGPL allows commercial use, on its own terms. The main ones:

- If you distribute the harness, changed or not, you do so under the same license, with its source.
- If you change the harness and let people use it over a network, you must offer those people the source of your changed version (section 13, "Remote Network Interaction").

A separate permission ([LICENSE-EXCEPTION.md](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/arena/LICENSE-EXCEPTION.md), under AGPL section 7) lets evaluation-standard plugins under other licenses work with the harness through its public plugin interface. It does not change the harness's own license.

## The Plains Cree plugin (`champollion-lyss`)

`champollion-lyss` has its own interim license: it may be used only with written permission. Permission is ordinarily granted without charge for noncommercial research, education and community-benefit use. No commercial use is permitted. It is an interim license, meant to be replaced by terms set through community governance. The license text and its NOTICE ship with the package.

## What these licenses do not cover

The translation services, models and corpora you use through these tools keep their own terms: a provider's API terms, a model's license, a corpus's license. The harness records each corpus's license and applies its rules on which model services may see it, but those terms are set by their owners, not by the licenses on this page.

## The license texts

- [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/cli/LICENSE) (also at [polyformproject.org](https://polyformproject.org/licenses/noncommercial/1.0.0)): the CLI, and the same text for the [MCP server](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/mcp-server/LICENSE) and [nmt-forge](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/forge/LICENSE)
- [GNU AGPL-3.0](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/arena/LICENSE) and its [plugin exception](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/blob/main/arena/LICENSE-EXCEPTION.md): the harness
- [champollion-lyss](https://pypi.org/project/champollion-lyss/): its interim license and NOTICE ship in the package

This page is a summary, not legal advice. Where it and a license text differ, the license text governs.

===== SECTION: The rails model =====

# The rails model

A project on the rails is a folder of plain files. Every tool — the
`champollion` CLI, `nmt-forge`, `mt-eval` and the MCP server — reads the same
files natively, against the same schemas, with the same verdicts. The next
step is always read from the files, never remembered. (Two things live
outside the project: the MCP server counts a step's failures for its own
lifetime, and nmt-forge keeps one machine-wide training queue in
`~/.nmt-forge`.) Change a file by hand, then ask for the next step, and the answer
reflects the change.

This page is the map. The operating rules are in
[the contract](/docs/agents/contract); the tool calls are in
[MCP](/docs/agents/mcp) and [the shell](/docs/agents/shell).

## The tools

| Tool | Install | What it does on the rails |
|---|---|---|
| `champollion` | npm (Node 20.11+) | Starts projects, brings data in, records its terms, names the next step, runs the improve rounds, connects a model to an app |
| `nmt-forge` | PyPI (`uv tool install --python 3.12 nmt-forge`) | Trains, screens, splits, records predictions, scores models on the test set and exports them, serves them; keeps the ledger |
| `mt-eval` | comes with `nmt-forge` (the `mt-eval-harness` package) | Runs a method over a test set, a file or a request; applies gates; scores |
| `champollion-mcp-server` | npx | Drives the `champollion` CLI as bounded child processes; the rails profile is six tools |

Each tool runs as its own process. The MCP server runs the same commands a
person types (its `run_next_step` refuses any program other than
`champollion`, `nmt-forge`, and `uv tool install … nmt-forge`).

## The project tree

`champollion new <folder> --from <language> --to <language>` writes:

```text
<folder>/
  champollion.project.json   project/1 — the decisions (kind, name, pair, purpose, defaults)
  README.md                  what goes where, for the people
  NEXT.md                    the next step, as a page (rewritten by `champollion next --write`)
  AGENTS.md                  the operating contract, for an AI agent working in the folder (an existing one is kept)
  .gitignore                 keeps data/, inbox/, consent/, models/, runs/, export*/, .forge/runs/, .champollion/ out of git
  inbox/                     files as the people have them
  data/parallel/             sentence pairs to learn from
  data/test/                 sentences a fluent speaker checked — never learned from
  data/lexicon/              word lists and dictionaries
  data/grammar/              grammar notes
  data/monolingual/          one-language text (kept; kept; not used for training)
  consent/                   notes recording who agreed to what, and when
```

It refuses a folder that already holds a project (exit 1) or any
non-hidden file (exit 1), and a `kind` other than `language`: `task` and
`service` projects are not on the rails yet. `--dry` resolves the languages
and writes nothing.

The steps add the rest as they run:

| Path | Written by | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `<file>.champollion.json` | `champollion data add`, `data mark`, `data combine`, `improve marks` | set/1 — the terms of the file beside it |
| `data/combined-from/` | `champollion data combine` | the originals combine joined (moved, never deleted) |
| `data/not-for-training/` | `champollion data combine` | files whose holders said no model may learn from them |
| `.forge/` | `nmt-forge init` | the workshop: `eval-registry.json`, `ledger.jsonl`, preregistrations, `runs/` |
| `config.json`, `NEXT_STEPS.md` | `nmt-forge init` | the training config (a model preset expanded into explicit numbers) |
| `data/clean/` | `nmt-forge leak-audit --clean-to` | the screened training pairs |
| `data/split/` | `nmt-forge split`, `champollion improve prepare` | the dev set; each round's training file |
| `data/dev/practice-round-<k>.tsv` | `champollion improve marks` | sentences the speaker wrote for the dev set — role `dev`, local-only, never trained on |
| `improve/time.json` | `champollion improve time` | the speaker's time, in their words |
| `improve/round-<k>/` | the improve steps | `wishlist.md`, `to-translate.txt`, `review.csv`, `sheet-key.json` (which rows the other model drafted — a newer one not in use, or the one a promotion replaced: row numbers, run names, the relation and each model's training-pair count — and, from round 2, `repeat_rows`: the rows shown again, each `row`, `from_round`, `from_row` and the earlier `mark`), `marks.json` (the counts, the share right with its interval, `blind`, and `repeats`: `shown`, `judged`, `agreed`, `agreement`, `wrong_to_right`, `right_to_wrong`, `wrong_before`, `rounds_apart_wrong_before`), `prepared.json`, `report.json` |
| `export*/` | `nmt-forge export` | an exported model and its method.json |
| `deploy/<name>.json` | `nmt-forge export` (inside a rails project) | deployment/1 — what is deployed |
| `gates/*.json` | people | gate-chain/1 — checks between output and what ships |
| `methods/<id>/method.json` | people | method/1 (also written by `nmt-forge export` into a model folder, `mt-eval export` and `champollion serve --emit-manifest`) |

## The formats

Six framework schemas live in `shared/schemas/framework/`. Each document
names its schema in `$schema`. Unknown keys are refused; a key of your own
goes under `x-`.

| Format | `$schema` | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| project/1 | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/project/1.json` | `champollion.project.json` | Decisions only: `kind`, `name`, `pair`, `purpose`, `defaults`, `created_with` |
| set/1 | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/set/1.json` | `<file>.champollion.json` | A data file's terms: `transmission`, `role`, `kind`, `pair`, `fields`, `terms`, registration fields, `derived_from`, `holders_agreed` |
| method/1 | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/method/1.json` | `method.json` | One method: `id`, `name`, `kind` and that kind's one setting, `pairs`, `decode`, `card`, `evidence` |
| gate-chain/1 | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/gate-chain/1.json` | `gates/*.json` | Ordered `metric-threshold` gates and an optional `fallback` |
| deployment/1 | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/deployment/1.json` | `deploy/*.json` | One method, its gates, one pair; optional `serve` host and port |
| service-api/1 | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/service-api/1.json` | the `/translate` contract | Request, response, error and `/health` documents |

`project.defaults` — what data added to the project gets when nobody says
otherwise. `champollion new` writes `{"transmission": "local-only",
"training": "ask", "share_scores": "ask"}`. The values: `transmission`
`local-only` or `ask`; `training` `allowed`, `not-allowed` or `ask`;
`share_scores` `never` or `ask`. `ask` makes the tools stop and ask — the rails
never invent an answer.

Two more records are not framework schemas but are part of the model:

- **The forge ledger**, `.forge/ledger.jsonl`: append-only and hash-chained
  (each entry embeds the hash of the one before; `nmt-forge ledger verify`
  fails on any edit). It records registrations, every read of a registered
  set, preregistrations, scores, sealed-set spends, overrides, leak-audit
  verdicts, the dictionary floor, exports, choices, serves, round verdicts
  (`improve-compare`: `better`, `worse`, `no-change`, or `too-few` under 50
  dev sentences), how each round trains (`round-plan`), the other model's
  drafts for a review sheet (`draft-newer`: run names, `relation`, each
  model's training-pair count and a count of drafts), the speaker's blind
  verdict on a newer model (`improve-speaker`: run names, four counts, `z`,
  `clear`), model changes (`model-change`, including a `not-now`) and what
  `nmt-forge tidy` removed (`tidy`: runs and bytes). Counts, hashes and
  paths — never a sentence. It is tamper-evident
  bookkeeping, not cryptographic security.
- **The run card**: what `mt-eval run` records for a scored run, and what a
  published result carries. See the [run card spec](/docs/network/specifications/run-card).

**Lock.** `champollion validate [folder]` checks the project file, every
sidecar, every `method.json` (at the root, in `methods/*/` and
`.champollion/methods/*/`), `gates/*.json` and `deploy/*.json` against these
schemas. The harness reads the same files with the same verdicts. Exit 0 = no
errors, 1 = a document is invalid, 2 = usage error. It opens only these JSON
files, never a data file.

`champollion upgrade [folder]` rewrites sidecars written before set/1 (no
`$schema`) as set/1, keeping every value (a key set/1 does not know moves
under `x-<key>`). It leaves an invalid sidecar alone, and lists an older
`method.json` without changing it: every tool still reads it, as method/0,
with a warning.

## The one pipeline

Every way a method meets text is one pipeline in the evaluation engine:

1. **Admit.** The input's terms are read (the set/1 sidecar, a JSON
   envelope, the registry entry) and its transmission policy is resolved and
   enforced before anything is translated. A channel the policy does not
   allow is refused here (see [data rules](/docs/agents/data-rules)).
2. **Method.** One method translates (method/1 kinds: `llm`, `llm-coached`,
   `mt-api`, `local-model`, `nmt-checkpoint`, `lexicon`, `python`, `service`,
   `human`).
3. **Gates.** If a gate chain is named, each segment is judged; the first gate
   that refuses decides what ships (`drop`, `keep-source`, `flag`,
   `fallback`). See [methods and gates](/docs/agents/methods).
4. **Outputs.** The run log is written; files carved from a marked input carry
   its terms in a sidecar beside them.
5. **Metrics.** Only when references exist: the headline scores what shipped,
   the ungated score sits beside it. See [measurement](/docs/agents/measurement).

The modes are the same pipeline on different input:

| Mode | Command | Input | Metrics |
|---|---|---|---|
| Measure | `mt-eval run` (`mt-eval test` re-scores a run log) | a test or dev set | yes |
| Translate a file | `mt-eval translate --out <file>` | source-only | no |
| Serve | `mt-eval serve` | one request at a time | no |

**A deployment is the measurement pipeline on source-only input.** One
deployment/1 file is tested (`mt-eval run --deployment`), run over a file
(`mt-eval translate --deployment`) and served (`mt-eval serve --deployment`),
so what was measured is what ships. With `--deployment`, the flags the file
decides (`--method`, `-m`/`--model`, `--gates`, `--target-script`) are refused.
A deployment names no score: a measured number is a run result, kept with the
run. See [serving](/docs/agents/serving).

## The journey, as data

The order of the work is a file: `shared/journeys/language.json`. The
evaluator, `cli/lib/framework/journey.js`, is the one reader;
`champollion next`, the MCP rails profile and `NEXT.md` all ask it the same
question. **The first step not done is the next step.** It reads only
sidecars, the project file and forge's registry and ledger — never a data
file's text — and runs nothing except `nmt-forge --version` (bounded at
30 s) for the install step and `nmt-forge status --json` (bounded at 60 s)
once the work reaches training.

**Stages.** `start` → `gather` → `protect` → `tools` → `build` → `improve`.

**A step** has an `id`, a `stage`, a `mode`, plain words to tell the person
(`say`) and why it matters (`why`), and usually a `command`. Optional fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `done_when` | The check that says the step is done. Required (except on a delegating step) |
| `when` | A check that must hold for the step to apply at all (the dictionary floor applies only when `data/lexicon/` holds a file) |
| `question`, `answers` | An `ask_user` step's question and its answer slots: `{"enum": [...]}` or `{"type": "string", "say": "…"}` |
| `agent`, `agent_tool` | What an agent does itself for a person's step (bring the named files in with `add_data`) |
| `outdated` | A variant used when the check finds the tool too old |
| `delegate` | `"nmt-forge"`: hand over to forge's own advisor |

`{placeholders}` in `say`, `question` and `command` are filled from the project
file and the files found.

**Checks** are a closed set; the evaluator throws on an unknown one:
`project_valid`, `data_files`, `every_data_file_has_terms`,
`protected_test_set`, `tool_on_path` (with `min_version`), `path_exists`,
`forge_test_registered`, `single_file`, `forge_role_registered`,
`forge_ledger_event`, `screened_rows`, `lines_in_file`, `review_marked`,
`improve_prepared`, `forge_trained_on_current`.

**Modes:**

| Mode | Who acts | What the rails allow |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` | the agent | run the command |
| `confirm` | the agent, after a yes | installs, training, anything that spends or publishes; run only after the person says yes |
| `ask_user` | the person answers | ask `question`; pass their answers by the keys in `answers`; never answer for them |
| `wait` | nobody | something is running; ask again later |
| `human_only` | a person | gather sentences, mark drafts, choose |
| `use_tool` | the agent, with its own tool | MCP only: a `human_only` step with an `agent` field is shown as `use_tool` with `step.tool` |

**Delegation.** At the `forge` step the journey asks `nmt-forge status
--json` and takes forge's state as the step. Forge's states map to modes:
`training` → `wait`; `ready-to-train` and `needs-training-extra` → `confirm`;
`missing-preregistration` → `ask_user`; `choose-export` → `human_only`;
`improve-compare` → `auto`; `improve-promote` → `confirm`;
`improve-stronger-model` → `ask_user`. Any other state is `auto` when forge
names a command, `human_only` when it does not. A state of `serving` ends the
build stage and the improve stage begins.

Two kinds of step come from outside the step list:

- **Judging the prediction.** After an export scored on the test set, a
  prediction the people wrote in their own words waits for their verdict: an
  `ask_user` step with `answers` `verdict` (`held` or `missed`) and `by` (who
  judged it), which runs `nmt-forge prereg verdict`.
- **Waiting for agreement.** Every file whose sidecar says `speakers_agreed:
  not-yet` becomes its own `ask_user` question in `waiting`, answered by its
  own step id whenever the person has the answer. It never holds up the rest
  of the rails.

**The step id** is `<journey step id>:<8 hex characters>` — a hash of the step
and its filled command. If the project changes, the id changes, and a
`run_next_step` with the old id is refused (`the project changed since that
step was named`).

**What `champollion next --json` returns:** `project`, `kind`, `stage` (`n`,
`of`, `id`, `title`), `done` (step ids), `step` (`id`, `mode`, `say`, `why`,
and where present `command`, `question`, `answers`, `agent`, `agent_tool`,
`file`, `source`), `now` (forge's facts — what is true right now), `waiting`,
`forge` (`state`, `blockers`, `warnings`), `finished` (when no step is left)
and `error`. Exit 1 when there is an error and no step.

## Refusal shapes

Every refusal says what happened, and most say why and the fix.

| Tool | Human output | Machine output | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nmt-forge` | `[guard] message`, then `  why: …` and `  fix: …` | `--json`: `{"error": {"type", "guard", "message", "why", "fix", "how_to_get", "text"}}` on stdout | 2 refused |
| `champollion` | `[ERR] message` on stderr | `--json` where the command supports it | 1 refused, 2 usage |
| MCP rails tools | — | `{"refused": "<reason>", …}` with `isError: true`, plus the retry where there is one (`if_it_has_no_code`, `current`, `last_output`, `question`, `answers`) | — |

`type` in forge's error is the exception class (`UsageError` for bad
arguments — forge refuses abbreviated flags rather than guess). Forge's guard
names include `split-guard`, `dev-fence`, `leak-audit`, `preregister`,
`eval-ledger`, `ci-scoring`, `registry`, `improve-loop` and `disk-room` (a
training run the disk cannot hold). When an error
would quote a sentence of a withheld corpus, the sentence reads
`[sentence withheld]` and the object adds `text_withheld`.

Relay a refusal in plain words and follow its fix, or ask for the next step
again. A step that failed twice is not run again until the person decides
([MCP](/docs/agents/mcp#when-a-step-fails)).

===== SECTION: Driving the rails over MCP =====

# Driving the rails over MCP

The MCP server's default profile is the rails: six tools that walk one
language project from an empty folder to a measured model on the person's
own computer. Each tool runs the `champollion` CLI as a separate, bounded
process — the same commands a person types. The server also hands your client
short operating instructions (`instructions-rails.md`) at connection time.

## Connect

The server speaks MCP over stdio and needs Node.js 20.11 or newer. The
configuration every file-configured client takes:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "champollion": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "champollion-mcp-server"] }
  }
}
```

| Client | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Claude desktop | Settings → Developer → Edit Config. Add the entry, save, restart the app |
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add champollion -- npx -y champollion-mcp-server` |
| Cursor | `mcp.json` in the project's `.cursor` folder, or in `.cursor` in the home folder |

Other clients that can start a local stdio server take the same command; this
page describes only the three above.

**Tool paths.** The server finds the CLI it depends on by itself. It finds
`nmt-forge` on `PATH`, then in `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR` (default `~/.local/bin`,
where `uv tool install` puts it) — a client launched from a desktop app often
has a shorter `PATH` than a terminal. Overrides, as environment variables in
the server entry's `env`:

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `CHAMPOLLION_MCP_PROFILE` | `rails` (default) or `full` |
| `CHAMPOLLION_CLI_BIN` | the `champollion` CLI entry point to run instead of the bundled one |
| `NMT_FORGE_BIN` | the `nmt-forge` executable (the CLI's journey honours the same variable) |
| `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR` | where to look for `nmt-forge` and `uv` after `PATH` |

## Profiles

| Profile | Select with | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| rails | the default | Six tools and short instructions; one language project, end to end |
| full | `--profile full` in `args`, or `CHAMPOLLION_MCP_PROFILE=full` | Every tool: language cards, corpora, benchmarks, the queue, contests, forge training, publishing |

Any other value stops the server: `unknown MCP profile "<value>" (rails or
full)`. The full set is catalogued on
[the MCP server page](/docs/network/getting-started/mcp-server). For a
language project, stay on the rails profile: it is the one whose every step
is read from the project's files.

## The loop

1. No project yet → `start_project`. Its first call makes nothing: say its
   `ask_first` to the person, then make the call it gives for their answer.
2. `project_status` → read `step.mode`, `step.say`, `step.why`.
3. Do what the mode says, using `step.call` — the exact call that takes the
   step.
4. Back to 2. After any change you or the person made by hand, call
   `project_status` again: the next step is always read from the files.
5. `step: null` → the rails are done. Tell the person what `finished` says.

| `step.mode` | Do this | `step.call` |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` | Run it | `run_next_step` with `project_dir`, `step_id` |
| `confirm` | Tell the person what it does (installs, training); ask yes or no; only on yes, run it. On "not now", record it: nothing runs | `run_next_step` with `confirmed: true` added after the yes; `declined: true` on "not now" |
| `ask_user` | Ask `step.question` in plain words; pass their answers by the keys in `step.answers`. On "not now": when `not-now` is one of a slot's own `enum` values, it is an answer — pass it; otherwise record it: nothing runs | `run_next_step` with `answers` — each slot written `<…>`, to be replaced by the person's words; `declined: true` on a "not now" that is not one of the answers |
| `wait` | Something is running | `project_status` with `wait_seconds: 120`; repeat while the mode stays `wait` |
| `use_tool` | You do it now with `step.tool`; do not hand it back | e.g. `add_data` with `path: "<each file the person named, where it is>"` |
| `human_only` | A person does it: tell them `step.say` | none |

`step.command` is what the rails run — never a tool name. A `<…>` in a call is
a slot for the person's answer or file; a slot sent back as it is gets
refused.

## The six tools

### `start_project`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string, required | New folder for the project, relative to `parent_dir` |
| `from` | string, required | The language people put in: a code or a name |
| `to` | string, required | The language that comes out: a code or a name |
| `target_name`, `source_name` | string | The language's name as its people say it; required for a private-use code (`qaa`–`qtz`) |
| `purpose` | string | What the translations are for, in the person's words |
| `parent_dir` | string | Where to create the folder (default: the server's working directory) |
| `confirmed` | boolean | `true` only after the person agreed to the direction |

Without `confirmed: true` it runs `champollion new --dry` and returns
`made: false`, `ask_first` (a sentence to say: *"This translator takes X and
gives back Y — you put X in, and Y comes out. Is that the way round you
want?"*), `if_yes` and `if_the_other_way` (each a complete call) and
`languages` — what each name resolved to, with `matchedAs` when the person's
word is another name a card records, and `alsoNamed` when the same word names
other languages. Say both back. With `confirmed: true` it makes the project
and returns `project`, `languages` and `next` (the first step).

A name no card carries and no close one: the refusal adds
`if_it_has_no_code`, the same call with `to: "qaa"` and their name as
`target_name`. Use it only for the name the person gave.

### `project_status`

Arguments: `project_dir` (required); `wait_seconds` (0–120). With
`wait_seconds`, it re-reads every 5 seconds while the step is `wait`, and
returns when the step changes or the time runs out.

Returns `project`, `stage` (`"2/6 Gather your data"`), `step` (`id`, `mode`,
`say`, `why`, `call`, and where present `question`, `answers`, `command`,
`tool`, `for_the_person`), and these when they apply:

| Field | What it is | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| `true_now` | Forge's own record, as sentences: models trained and their best dev chrF++, the leak audit's verdict per test set, test-set scores, whether training is running, whether a model is served and where | Say what has been done only from these lines, never more |
| `waiting_for_agreement` | Files whose speakers have not agreed yet (`speakers_agreed: not-yet`): each with `file`, `question`, `say` and its own `call` | Ask each question once a session, gently; make its call only when the person says everyone agreed |
| `files_not_added` | Files `add_data` refused this session that are still not in the project, each with its refusal | Bring each in (its refusal says how), or tell the person which is left out and why |
| `model_in_use` | Once a model is served, beside the improve rounds' steps: `say` (its try page and how it is used) and `for_the_person` (the `champollion connect` command that puts it into their app or website) | Tell the person once; they run connect when they want it |
| `blockers`, `warnings` | Forge's, verbatim | Pass them on word for word |
| `finished` | When no step is left: what the people can do now (try the model on its page; an app) | Tell the person |
| `error` | Why no step could be named | Relay it |

A project folder that does not exist, or has no `champollion.project.json`,
is refused with the projects found nearby.

### `run_next_step`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `project_dir` | string, required | The project folder |
| `step_id` | string, required | The `step.id` (or a `waiting_for_agreement` entry's id) just returned |
| `answers` | object of strings | `ask_user`: the person's answers by the keys in `step.answers` |
| `confirmed` | boolean | `confirm`: `true` only after the person said yes. Also: a step that failed twice, only when the person says to try it again as it is |
| `declined` | boolean | `true` when the person said not now to a `confirm` step, or to a question with no `not-now` answer of its own: nothing runs, and it is not asked again this session. Where `not-now` is one of the answers, pass it in `answers` |

It reads the next step again before it runs anything. **Locks:**

- A different id is refused: `the project changed since that step was named
  — call project_status again`, with `current`.
- `human_only` is refused (`a person does this step: …`); a `human_only` step
  an agent does with a tool is refused with the tool to use.
- `wait` is refused; `confirm` without `confirmed: true` is refused (`ask the
  person first, then call again with confirmed: true`).
- `ask_user`: every answer is required (`missing the answer "<key>" — ask the
  person who holds the data; never answer for them`); a `<…>` placeholder is
  refused; an answer outside an `enum` is refused.
- Only the rails' own programs run: `champollion`, `nmt-forge`, and `uv tool
  install … nmt-forge`. A command using `|`, `;`, `<`, `>`, `` ` ``, `$` or a
  lone `&` is refused; `&&` joins parts, run in order, stopping at the first
  failure.
- Each part is bounded at 10 minutes (the `uv` install at 15).
- `declined: true` on a step that is neither `confirm` nor `ask_user` is
  refused: `this step does not wait on the person's yes (<mode>) — there is
  nothing to decline`.
- `declined: true` on a step whose `answers` include `not-now` (today, the
  stronger-model offer's `try_it`) is refused, and the refusal carries the
  step's `answers`: `"not now" is one of this step's own answers — pass it in
  answers (try_it: "not-now"): it is recorded, and this comes back only after
  more rounds; declined would ask again next session`.

Returns `ran` — per part: `command`, `exit_code`, `timed_out` when it did, and
the last 40 lines of `output` — and `next`, the next step in
`project_status`'s shape.

#### "Not now"

There are two ways to record it, and the step decides which:

| The step | "Not now" is | What it records | When it comes back |
|---|---|---|---|
| An `ask_user` step whose `answers` include `not-now` (the stronger-model offer: `try_it`, `yes` or `not-now`) | An answer: `answers: {"try_it": "not-now"}` | Forge's ledger (`model-change`, `answer: "not-now"`); nothing else changes | After two more rounds the dev set judged **no-change** or **worse** — across sessions |
| A `confirm` step (training, an install, putting a model to use), or a question the person can't answer yet | `declined: true` | This server's memory only | When the server restarts (the next session) |

`declined: true` runs nothing and returns `declined` (the step id), `ran: []`,
`say` (*"Nothing ran. It is not asked again this session; if they bring it up
and say yes, take it then."*) and `next`. The decline is kept for the
server's life — one session; a restarted server has forgotten it. While it
stands, that step comes back from `project_status` and `run_next_step` with
`declined_this_session` (when, as an ISO time) and its `say` beginning *"They
said not now (HH:MM UTC) to this: …"* and ending *"Do not ask again this
session — nothing that needs their yes runs. If they bring it up themselves
and say yes, take it with confirmed: true (or their answers)."* A later
`confirmed: true`, or answers, takes the step and clears the decline.
**Note.** Don't ask again this session, and don't route around the step; if
the person brings it up and says yes, take it then.

#### When a step fails

**Lock.** A step that failed twice in a row (non-zero exit or timeout, counted
for the server's lifetime) is refused a third time unless `confirmed: true`,
with its `last_output`. **Note.** That flag is yours to set: tell the person
what it said, and either they fix it (a corrected command run in a terminal is
fine — then call `project_status`), or they say to try again as it is.

### `add_data`

| Argument | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `project_dir` | string, required | The project folder |
| `path` | string, required | The file where it is: absolute, or relative to the project folder or to where the server started |
| `into` | `parallel` (default) · `test` · `lexicon` | Pairs to learn from; the checked test sentences; a word list |
| `source_col`, `target_col` | string | A column as a letter (`A`), a number, or its header; for ELAN, the tier number the refusal lists (or an exact tier id the person typed); for LIFT, a language code |
| `sheet` | string | Which sheet or table, when there are several |
| `header` | boolean | `true`: the first row is a header; `false`: it is data |
| `usfm_source` | string | USFM scripture only: the other language's text (a `.usfm` file or folder) |
| `replace` | boolean | Read a file already added again (another header or columns); its holders' answers are kept |

It runs `champollion data add`. Call it with just the path first: a header
naming the pair's languages decides the columns; otherwise it asks, and you
ask the person — never decide from the content. It reads spreadsheets
(`.xlsx`, `.ods`, `.csv`), `.tsv` and `.txt`, tables in Word `.docx`, Toolbox
and LIFT dictionaries, ELAN `.eaf` files and USFM.

Returns `result` (the CLI's report: counts, columns, ELAN tiers by number, and
the row numbers its check of the rows names — copies, repeats, odd lengths,
swapped or shifted rows, nothing removed — never sentences), `read_from` when
the file was found from the server's starting folder, and `also` when the
file holds more (a dictionary's example sentences as pairs, or its glosses as
a word list) — each entry a complete `add_data` call. Make it unless the
person's terms for that file rule it out. Pass the row check on as it is: the
person looks at those rows in their own file
([data rules](/docs/agents/data-rules#what-tools-print-and-never-print)).
Never ask the person to move a file; `inbox/` is only a place they may drop
one.

### `try_translation`

Arguments: `project_dir`; `text` — up to 10 lines, at most 2,000 characters,
one sentence per line, words the person gave you.

It finds the model this project serves (the newest healthy `serve` job in
`nmt-forge jobs --json`), on this computer only, and reads its `/health`.

- **Lock.** If `output_local_only` is not `false` (true, or unknown), it
  returns no translation: `shown_to_person_only: true`, `open` (the model's
  own page) and `say`. Send the person there; do not ask them to paste its
  translations back to you.
- A server that asks for a token is refused: tokens are never handed to an
  agent.
- Otherwise it returns `model`, `pair`, `translations` (`source`,
  `translation` per line), `errors` if any, and `say`: pass them on as they
  are; the server checks nothing it returns.

### `explain`

Argument: `topic`. Plain-words texts to pass on:

| `topic` | Covers |
|---|---|
| `rails` | The project folder and the order of the steps |
| `privacy` | What the sidecar means; why you never open the files |
| `quality` | What a score promises and does not |
| `modes` | How to take each kind of step |
| `improve` | The rounds after a model is in use: about one review row in ten *"comes back from an earlier sheet on purpose (the sheet says so …)"*; a better model is offered for use and the people say yes (*"a verdict alone changes nothing"*); the too-few verdict; the stronger-model offer after *"two rounds in a row that the dev set could judge show no gain (counted from the last model put to use)"* |
| `off_rails` | Stepping off: run an expert command, then call `project_status` |

## Notes for the whole session

- **Note.** Everything you read goes to your model provider. `add_data`,
  `project_status` and `run_next_step` report counts, columns and states, never
  sentences; keep it that way. Do not open the files yourself.
- **Note.** The `ask_user` answers, `confirmed: true` and the
  `waiting_for_agreement` yes are the person's. The tools check that an answer
  is present and well-formed; only you can make sure it is theirs.
- **Note.** Relay `blockers`, `warnings` and every caveat word for word, and
  every number with its unit and the set it was measured on
  ([coaching](/docs/agents/coaching)).

- [The operating contract](/docs/agents/contract) — locks and notes.
- [The rails model](/docs/agents/rails-model) — the journey, the modes and the
  step ids these tools read.

  commands.
- [The MCP server](/docs/network/getting-started/mcp-server) — both profiles
  and the full tool catalogue.

===== SECTION: Driving the rails from the shell =====

# Driving the rails from the shell

Every step on the rails is an ordinary command. An agent without MCP — or a
person at a terminal — walks the same rails with three programs:
`champollion`, `nmt-forge` and `mt-eval`. The order never has to be
remembered: `champollion next` names the next step, with its mode and the
exact command, read from the project's files.

The rules are the same as over MCP. A `confirm` step runs only after the
person says yes; an `ask_user` step's answers are theirs
([the contract](/docs/agents/contract)).

## Install

```bash
npm install -g champollion                  # Node.js 20.11 or newer
uv tool install --python 3.12 nmt-forge     # brings mt-eval (mt-eval-harness) with it
```

**Note.** Both download packages: `confirm` mode — ask first. If `uv
--version` fails, the person installs uv from https://docs.astral.sh/uv/;
an agent does not download installers. Training also needs forge's training
extra (PyTorch and Hugging Face transformers, several hundred MB). Forge names
it when it is missing (state `needs-training-extra`):

```bash
uv tool install --reinstall --python 3.12 'nmt-forge[hf]'
```

The rails need `nmt-forge` 0.3.0 or newer; an older one is named with its
upgrade command (`uv tool install --upgrade --python 3.12 nmt-forge`).

## The loop

```bash
champollion next              # the next step: what to say, why, the command, how to take it
champollion next --json       # the same, for a program (see the rails model page for the shape)
champollion next --write      # also rewrite NEXT.md, the person's copy
```

`How:` in the human output is the mode: `run it` (`auto`), `ask first, then
run it` (`confirm`), `ask the person who holds the data — never answer for
them` (`ask_user`), `wait, then ask again` (`wait`), `a person does this`
(`human_only`). Run the command it names, then ask again. Stepping off the
rails is fine — run any expert command, then `champollion next`: the next step
is read from the files.

## Start

```bash
champollion new family --from English --to qaa --target-name "Our language" --dry
champollion new family --from English --to qaa --target-name "Our language" --purpose "notes for the grandchildren"
cd family
```

Languages are codes or names, resolved through the language cards. A variety
with no code takes a private-use code (`qaa`–`qtz`) and the name its people
give (`--target-name`, `--source-name`). **Note.** Say the direction back
before the project is made: `--dry` resolves both languages and writes
nothing. Pass each language exactly as the person named it.

## Gather and record terms

```bash
champollion data add ../family-files/grandpa.xlsx                     # pairs → data/parallel/
champollion data add ../family-files/grandpa.xlsx --source-col A --target-col B --header
champollion data add ../family-files/words.lift --into lexicon        # a word list → data/lexicon/
champollion data add ../family-files/recording.eaf --source-col <number> --target-col <number>   # ELAN: tier numbers
```

`data add` reads `.xlsx`, `.ods`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`, Word `.docx`
tables, Toolbox and LIFT dictionaries, ELAN `.eaf` and USFM
(`--usfm-source`). It writes `<stem>.tsv` and its sidecar, leaves the original
untouched, and prints counts, columns and the row numbers its check of the
rows names (copies, repeats, odd lengths, swapped or shifted rows — nothing
is removed) — never sentences. When it cannot tell which column (or ELAN
tier, by number, or LIFT language) is which, it refuses and asks; ask the
person. `--replace` reads the same original again with other columns, keeping
the holders' answers; `--name <stem>` adds another file under another name.
See [data rules](/docs/agents/data-rules#what-tools-print-and-never-print).

Then the terms, one file at a time, from the person's answers:

```bash
champollion data mark data/parallel/grandpa.tsv --speakers "grandpa" --speakers-agreed yes \
  --owner "our family" --training allowed --local-only
```

`--local-only` or `--may-leave` is required on a file not yet local-only.
The journey's terms step asks about each file in `data/parallel/`,
`data/lexicon/`, `data/grammar/` and `data/monolingual/` until both its
training answer and `--speakers-agreed` are recorded. Every value is the
holders' — see [data rules](/docs/agents/data-rules) for what each does and
what the command refuses.

## Protect the test set

```bash
champollion data add ../family-files/checked.tsv --into test
champollion data mark data/test/checked.tsv --role test --training not-allowed --local-only
```

## Build and test a model

The journey names these in order (their `{placeholders}` filled from the
project):

```bash
nmt-forge init qaa --dir . --pair eng-qaa --no-card --name "Our language" --model auto
nmt-forge registry add project-test data/test/checked.tsv --role test
champollion data combine
nmt-forge leak-audit data/parallel/combined.tsv --clean-to data/clean/combined.clean.jsonl
nmt-forge prereg new first-model --eval-set project-test --expect "<their words>" --rationale "<their reason>"
nmt-forge split data/clean/combined.clean.jsonl --test 0 --dev 50 --seed 42 --near-dupe 0.6 --max-group 26 --out data/split --register project
nmt-forge floor data/lexicon/words.tsv
```

- `init --model auto` picks the strongest model this computer can train in
  hours, by its memory ([training](/docs/agents/training#models)). With a
  language card, `--no-card --name` is left out.
- `data combine` runs only when `data/parallel/` holds more than one file. It
  keeps the strictest terms of the files it joins and refuses a file whose
  holders have not answered yet — whether a model may learn from it, and
  whether everyone whose words are in it agreed.
- `prereg new` is an `ask_user` step: `--expect` and `--rationale` are the
  people's words, exactly as they said them, written before any score exists.
  The question suggests no number, and neither do you.
- The dev size the journey fills in (`dev_n`) is one in ten of the screened
  pairs, at least 50 and at most 500; with fewer than 200 pairs it is a
  quarter of them instead, so training keeps most — and that is under 50.
  So: 40 dev sentences from 160 pairs, 50 from 200 to 500 pairs, 160 from
  1,600, 500 from 5,000 or more. Under 50, no round can be judged on the dev
  set ([measurement](/docs/agents/measurement#comparing-two-models)).
  `--near-dupe 0.6` keeps near-copies on one side; `--max-group` is half the
  dev size, rounded down, plus one.
- `floor` applies only when `data/lexicon/` holds a word list.

From here, forge's own advisor names each step. `champollion next` relays it;
`nmt-forge status` says it directly:

```bash
nmt-forge preflight run --config config.json && nmt-forge run config.json --detach
nmt-forge jobs                      # what is running
nmt-forge status                    # the next step, with what is ready and what blocks it
nmt-forge export <run-manifest.json> --prereg first-model --out export/
nmt-forge serve export/model --detach
nmt-forge tidy                      # earlier rounds' model weights nothing uses, and the space they take
```

Training is `confirm` (it spends compute, minutes to hours); while a detached
run trains, the step is `wait`. `nmt-forge run` refuses a run the disk cannot
hold before it starts (`[disk-room]`), with the free space, its estimate and
what `nmt-forge tidy` would free; `nmt-forge tidy --yes` frees it, and
`--skip-disk-check` on `run` starts anyway, recorded in the run. Those two are
the person's call, not yours ([training](/docs/agents/training#disk-space)).
The export scores the model once on the test set, against the prediction.
Choosing among several exports is the person's
(`nmt-forge choose <model folder>`). After a test-set score, the people judge
their prediction:

```bash
nmt-forge prereg verdict first-model --prediction 1 --held --by "grandma"
```

(`--missed` when it did not hold; `--prediction` is the prediction's number,
1 for a single `--expect`; `--by` names who judged it, as they said.) See
[training](/docs/agents/training) for every forge command and refusal.

## The improve rounds

Once a model is served, rounds begin:

```bash
champollion improve time --per-week "about 30 sentences" --total "maybe 800"
champollion improve wishlist        # improve/round-<k>/wishlist.md, a printable sheet
# the people write 20 or more sentences in improve/round-<k>/to-translate.txt
champollion improve sheet           # the model in use drafts them → improve/round-<k>/review.csv
# the speaker marks the Right? column: Y, N (and how it is said), or ?
champollion improve marks           # counts the marks; fixes and confirmed drafts become pairs
champollion improve report          # the round's report
champollion improve prepare         # grows the dev set, screens, points config.json at the round's file, plans the training
nmt-forge preflight run --config config.json && nmt-forge run config.json --detach
champollion improve status          # the rounds so far: marks, and each verdict in the round report's words
```

- `improve sheet`: while the dev (practice) set is under 200 sentences, some
  rows have no draft — one in two while it is under 50, one in four from 50
  — and the speaker writes them. `improve marks` writes them to `data/dev/`
  and `improve prepare` adds them to the dev set (`nmt-forge grow-dev`),
  never to training. It also runs `nmt-forge draft-newer`. When there is
  another model — the newest trained one when it is not in use (not put to
  use after its round: too few to tell, no measurable change, or worse), or,
  after a promotion, the model the one in use replaced — that model drafts a
  random half of the drafted rows, unmarked, and the key stays beside the
  sheet (`sheet-key.json`). `improve marks` then counts each model apart —
  the blind comparison, which after a promotion is the check the report
  needs before it calls a rise real progress
  ([measurement](/docs/agents/measurement#the-speakers-marks)).
- `improve sheet`, from round 2: one row for every 10 new sentences
  (rounded down) is a draft the speaker marked `Y` or `N` on an earlier
  sheet, back unmarked at a random place. The sheet's first line says a few
  rows come back on purpose, never which; `sheet-key.json` lists them
  (`repeat_rows`). The command prints how many came back, *"(which ones is
  not marked)"*, and that they take *"about 10 seconds a row, never trained
  on again"*.
- `improve marks` judges a row shown again only against the speaker's
  earlier mark — never in the round's share, the training pairs or the
  blind comparison — writes `repeats` into `marks.json`, and prints *"Rows
  shown again: the speaker marked A of J the way they did before (P%) — W
  once wrong now right, R once right now wrong. Not counted in this round's
  share, and not trained on again."*
- `improve marks`, when the other model is the newer one and the speaker
  judged at least one draft of each, records the counts with forge (counts
  only, never a sentence):

  ```bash
  nmt-forge speaker-verdict --newer <run> --in-use <run> --newer-right <n> --newer-judged <n> --in-use-right <n> --in-use-judged <n> --json
  ```

  When the speaker marked the newer model right clearly more often, it
  prints *"forge recorded it: it offers to put the newer model to use (the
  people say yes first)"*; when forge is not installed or refuses, it says
  that the marks were not recorded, and why.
- `improve prepare` ends with `nmt-forge round-plan`: the round continues
  from the model in use (4 passes over all the sentences so far) or trains
  from the start, and says why ([training](/docs/agents/training#the-improve-rounds)).

Forge then judges the new model against the one in use
(`nmt-forge compare-runs <in-use run-manifest.json> <new run-manifest.json>`,
`auto`), and offers to put it to use (`confirm`) only if it is measurably
better — or, where the verdict was too few to tell (under 50 dev sentences)
or no measurable change, once the speaker's blind marks clearly preferred
it. A verdict alone puts nothing to use: only the people's yes (that step's
`nmt-forge export` and `nmt-forge choose`) does. The new pairs from `improve marks` get their own terms first — the
journey asks. How to relay the report: [coaching](/docs/agents/coaching).

## Translate and serve with mt-eval

`nmt-forge export` inside a project writes `deploy/<name>.json` (deployment/1).
The same file measures, translates and serves:

```bash
mt-eval translate --deployment deploy/<name>.json --source-file <input file> --out <output file>
mt-eval serve --deployment deploy/<name>.json      # http://127.0.0.1:8379 by default
mt-eval run --deployment deploy/<name>.json --corpus <dev or test file>
```

- **Note.** `mt-eval run` on a test file needs no preregistration — it only
  logs the read. Score the test set through `nmt-forge export` (or after the
  prediction is written), never before.
- `--gates gates/<chain>.json` adds a gate chain to `run`, `translate` or
  `serve` (without `--deployment`); `run` and `test` refuse a chain that falls
  back. See [methods and gates](/docs/agents/methods) and
  [serving](/docs/agents/serving).

## Off the rails: what exists for a language

```bash
champollion network card <code>                    # the cited language card
champollion network recommend <source> <target>    # methods that can run, with their evidence
mt-eval corpora --source <source> --target <target>   # registered test sets for the pair
nmt-forge discover <code>                          # what a training project can use
```

## Check and upgrade the files

```bash
champollion validate        # project file, sidecars, method.json, gates/, deploy/ — 0 ok, 1 invalid, 2 usage
champollion upgrade --dry   # what upgrading older sidecars to set/1 would change; drop --dry to write
```

## Offline

`CHAMPOLLION_OFFLINE=1` stops the `champollion` CLI from touching the network:
language cards come only from the bundled set and the local cache (a
long-tail card is not fetched), the daily card-cache refresh is skipped, and
`register-corpus` does not compare a file's hash with the public catalogue
(it records the comparison as not made). It does not change what a method
sends: a method that calls a provider still needs the network, and the
transmission rules still apply.

`MT_EVAL_NO_REMOTE_REGISTRY=1` stops `mt-eval` fetching its dataset registry
from the web (for an air-gapped machine).

What needs the network on the rails regardless: installing the tools, the
training extra, and a pretrained model's first download (`byt5-small` or
`byt5-small-lowmem`, about 1.2 GB; `cpu-tiny` downloads nothing).

## Environment variables

Read by the code, for an operator. Provider API keys are needed only by
methods that call a provider, never on the rails' default path.

| Variable | Read by | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `CHAMPOLLION_MCP_PROFILE` | MCP server | `rails` (default) or `full` |
| `CHAMPOLLION_CLI_BIN` | MCP server | The `champollion` entry point to run |
| `NMT_FORGE_BIN` | `champollion`, MCP server | The `nmt-forge` executable |
| `UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR` | `champollion`, MCP server | Where to look for `nmt-forge` and `uv` after `PATH` (default `~/.local/bin`) |
| `CHAMPOLLION_OFFLINE` | `champollion` | `1`: no network for cards or catalogue lookups |
| `CHAMPOLLION_CARDS_CACHE_DIR` | `champollion` | The per-user card cache (default `~/.champollion/cards`) |
| `CHAMPOLLION_CARDS_TTL_HOURS` | `champollion` | How often the card cache is checked for updates (default 24) |
| `NMT_FORGE_AUTO_PRESET` | `nmt-forge init --model auto` | Pins the preset `auto` picks (must be a preset name) |
| `NMT_FORGE_SERVE_PORT` | `nmt-forge serve` | Default port (8378 without it) |
| `NMT_FORGE_SERVE_TOKEN` | `nmt-forge serve` | The bearer token; required off loopback |
| `NMT_FORGE_NO_MONITOR` | `nmt-forge run` | `1`: no live training panel |
| `MT_EVAL_SERVE_TOKEN` | `mt-eval serve` | The bearer token (never a command-line value) |
| `CHAMPOLLION_SERVE_TOKEN` | `champollion serve` | The bearer token for the CLI's own server |
| `MT_EVAL_NO_REMOTE_REGISTRY` | `mt-eval` | `1`: no registry fetch |
| `MT_EVAL_DATA_ROOT` | `mt-eval` | Where registered datasets' paths are resolved first |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | `champollion`, `mt-eval` | The default hosted-model provider's key |

## Output for programs

| Tool | Machine output | Exit codes |
|---|---|---|
| `champollion` | `--json` on the rails commands (`new`, `next`, `data add`, `data mark`, `data combine`, `improve report`, `improve status`, `connect`, `upgrade`) | 0 ok · 1 refused · 2 usage |
| `nmt-forge` | `--json` on every subcommand: one JSON document on stdout, everything else on stderr | 0 ok · 2 refused (`{"error": …}`) |
| `mt-eval` | `--json` and `--non-interactive` on every subcommand | 0 ok · non-zero refused |

Refusal shapes: [the rails model](/docs/agents/rails-model#refusal-shapes).
