### `mt-eval node ceremony`

Key ceremony for a sealed set: generate + split the set key M-of-N on the offline node, distribute shares, verify by test reconstruction, restore only into executor memory — champollion.dev/docs/network/sovereignty/sovereign-eval-node

Subcommands: [`init`](#mt-eval-node-ceremony-init), [`share`](#mt-eval-node-ceremony-share), [`verify`](#mt-eval-node-ceremony-verify), [`restore`](#mt-eval-node-ceremony-restore).

#### `mt-eval node ceremony init`

Generate the set key, split M-of-N, write the public ceremony record + share files; the key itself is zeroed in the same call and never persists

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dir` | `DIR` |  | **Required.** Ceremony directory to create |
| `--set` | `SET_ID` |  | **Required.** Sealed-set/card id the key will seal |
| `--group` | `GROUP` |  | **Required.** Custodian group id (recorded on the card) |
| `--quorum`, `--m` | `M` | `3` | Quorum size M — how many custodians must present a share to open the set (default 3). `--m` is an accepted alias |
| `--shares`, `--n` | `N` | `5` | Share count N — how many custodian shares the key is split into (default 5). `--n` is an accepted alias |
| `--custodian` | `CUSTODIANS` |  | Custodian name (repeat n times; defaults to custodian-1..n) |

#### `mt-eval node ceremony share`

List/emit custodian shares from the ceremony dir; copy one to a token with --custodian + --dest; wipe the originals once distribution is verified

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dir` | `DIR` |  | **Required.** Ceremony directory |
| `--custodian` | `CUSTODIAN` |  | Which custodian's share to emit |
| `--dest` | `DEST` |  | Copy the share (+ printable .txt) here |
| `--qr` | switch |  | Also render a QR (needs the optional 'qrcode' package) |
| `--all-shares-i-understand` | switch |  | Emit/render EVERY share at once (defeats M-of-N — only for a single-holder recovery you accept the risk of). Normally emit one share per --custodian. |
| `--wipe-originals` | switch |  | Overwrite-then-delete the ceremony dir's share files (after distribution + verify) |

#### `mt-eval node ceremony verify`

Test reconstruction from ≥M shares against the ceremony record — nothing is persisted

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dir` | `DIR` |  | **Required.** Ceremony directory (or ceremony.json) |
| `--share` | `SHARES` |  | **Required.** Share file (repeat ≥M times) |

#### `mt-eval node ceremony restore`

Quorum-reconstruction drill: rebuild the key in locked memory, check the commitment, zero it — proves the quorum works without persisting anything

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--share` | `SHARES` |  | **Required.** Share file (repeat ≥M times) |
| `--expect-key-id` | `EXPECT_KEY_ID` |  | Expected key id (e.g. from the sealed artifact or ceremony record) |
| `--i-understand-this-assembles-the-key` | switch |  | Required acknowledgement: `restore` reconstructs the REAL set key in memory (unlike a sealed run, which does it inside the executor and consumes a grant). This standalone drill is unlogged — only run it during a ceremony sitting. |

### `mt-eval node seal`

Seal a corpus to a ceremony's public key: ciphertext artifact + content-free card block; the platform stores ciphertext + metadata, never plaintext (M1)

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--corpus` | `CORPUS` |  | **Required.** Plaintext corpus file |
| `--pubkey` | `PUBKEY` |  | **Required.** Ceremony record / pub.json / base64 SPKI DER |
| `--card-id` | `CARD_ID` |  | **Required.** Sealed-set card id |
| `--group` | `GROUP` |  | **Required.** Custodian group id |
| `--out-dir` | `OUT_DIR` | `.` | Where the artifact + card block are written |
| `--key-scheme` | `KEY_SCHEME` |  | Custody scheme label (defaults to the pubkey file's keyScheme, e.g. shamir-gf256-3-of-5) |

### `mt-eval node keygen`

Generate the node's Ed25519 score-signing keypair (same file format as `champollion network seal-corpus sign-keygen`; publish the .pub.json)

| Option | Takes | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--out` | `OUT` | `.` | Output directory |

# forge Command Reference

Every `nmt-forge` subcommand, generated directly from the CLI parser so this
page cannot drift from the tool. For the *why* behind each guard and for
driving forge from an agent, see
[Training with nmt-forge](/docs/agents/training); for the plain-words story, see
[Your first translator](/docs/your-first-translator).

**The global flag:** `--workspace <dir>` (default `./.forge`) precedes every
subcommand and names the project you are operating on.

Agents: call `nmt-forge status --json` first — it tells you which of these to
run next.

## `discover`

what does this language have? (reads the language card through the eval harness's resolver; absence = unknown, never zero)

**Arguments:**

- `code` — ISO 639-3 code (e.g. crk, fra, nav, arb)

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--cards-dir` — a directory of &lt;code>.json language cards (e.g. exported with `champollion network card <code> --json`). Default: $MT_EVAL_CARDS_DIR / $CHAMPOLLION_CARDS_DIR, a checkout or node_modules/champollion above the working directory, else the public card index (cached; reused offline)
- `--no-registry` — skip the mt-eval registry cross-check of eval datasets

## `init`

scaffold a project from a language card: workspace + starter config + NEXT_STEPS.md

**Arguments:**

- `code` — ISO 639-3 code of the TARGET language

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--dir` — project directory (default .)
- `--pair` — language pair: eng-crk, or 'eng>crk' (quote the > form — an unquoted > is a shell redirect) (default eng-&lt;code>)
- `--cards-dir` — a directory of &lt;code>.json language cards (see `discover --help`)
- `--model` (one of: byt5-small, byt5-small-lowmem, cpu-finetune, cpu-tiny, nllb-600m, auto) — model preset (default cpu-tiny; auto: byt5-small where there is a GPU forge can train on, else cpu-tiny, said why) — cpu-tiny: tiny transformer trained from scratch on your pairs — CPU, no download, minutes; weak by design, honest loop; cpu-finetune: fine-tune a small pretrained Marian/opus-mt model on CPU — ~300 MB download; usually stronger than cpu-tiny when a RELATED pair exists (you name the base); nllb-600m: NLLB-200 distilled 600M with LoRA — strongest start, needs a GPU (~2.5 GB download); byt5-small: Google's ByT5-small (300M parameters, reads bytes — no vocabulary to fit) fine-tuned on your pairs — ~1.2 GB download; Apple silicon or a GPU makes it hours, not days; byt5-small-lowmem: Google's ByT5-small (300M parameters, reads bytes — no vocabulary to fit) fine-tuned on your pairs — ~1.2 GB download; Apple silicon or a GPU makes it hours, not days — set up for a computer with 8–15 GB of memory (less memory per step, more time)
- `--no-card` — scaffold a language the card index doesn't have yet (everything a card would say is then unknown)
- `--name` — the language's name (with --no-card)
- `--base` — pretrained model for --model cpu-finetune (a Hugging Face id or a local dir, e.g. an opus-mt model for a RELATED pair); optional override for nllb-600m

## `status`

where am I? state table + THE next command (agents: call this first, use --json)

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2

## `preflight`

will &lt;command> refuse? every gate it will hit, with fixes (exit 2 if any gate fails)

**Arguments:**

- `target` — command to preflight: run|evaluate|export|serve|score|split|prereg|leak-audit

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--config` — run config for run/evaluate/export (default ./config.json) — checks it parses, its dev set, its data files, and that the backend's extra is installed

## `lint`

diagnose a battery manifest: weak registers → likeliest cause → the lever to pull next; every caveat mt-eval wrote on the same read's TestReport (a near-constant output, length, copies) is a finding, beside the headline chrF++ and its CI

**Arguments:**

- `manifest` — battery manifest json (guard: ci-scoring/battery); an export's is `<export>/evaluation/battery-hyps-battery.json`. A run's run-manifest.json lints the battery of every scored export of that run (refused, with the export command, when it has none)

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--run-manifest` — run manifest for schedule/transfer-plateau signals

## `split`

group-disjoint train/dev/test carve

**Arguments:**

- `corpus` — 

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--test` *(required)* — test rows to carve (≥ 0). Use 0 when your test set is a SEPARATE file (teacher-checked, private): register it with `registry add <name> <file> --role test` and carve only train/dev
- `--dev` — dev rows to carve (checkpoint selection runs on these; training refuses without a dev set)
- `--seed` *(required)* — 
- `--out` *(required)* — 
- `--source-field` — 
- `--target-field` — 
- `--register` — also register PREFIX-test / PREFIX-dev in the workspace
- `--allow-rotate` — with --register: replace PREFIX-dev / PREFIX-test when they are already registered with other content (e.g. re-splitting after leak-audit --clean-to). The rotation is ledgered with what it replaced and how often that content was read; without the flag a conflicting split is refused before any file is written
- `--near-dupe` — also keep NEAR-duplicates on one side (e.g. 0.6): rows whose source or target words overlap at ≥ this Jaccard are grouped, so sentences built on the same template/frame never straddle train and test. Use it when the split reports test rows with a near-twin in training. Templates can chain into one huge group on a small templated corpus: when a side would get far more rows than asked (over 1.5x), split refuses and says what to do
- `--max-group` — with --near-dupe: cap near-duplicate share-groups at N rows (strongest links first), so templates that chain cannot form one giant group. Exact-duplicate groups are never capped. Near-duplicate links left uncut are counted, and the split's near-twin check reports the twins that cross sides

## `verify-split`

zero-overlap check on existing files

**Arguments:**

- `sides` — train/dev/test files (any subset)

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--source-field` — 
- `--target-field` — 

## `leak-audit`

screen a corpus vs registered evals — explains what it would drop (exact / near-duplicate answers) and what it keeps on purpose (template siblings; a NEAR-duplicate prompt with a different answer — an IDENTICAL prompt is dropped), with examples; deterministic. With a fixed test set, --drop-test-twins also drops the training rows that are near-twins of it

**Arguments:**

- `corpus` — 

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2
- `--strict` — hard-fail on test/sealed hits
- `--clean-to` — write surviving rows here (plus an audit manifest next to it)
- `--drop-test-twins` — with --clean-to: ALSO drop the training rows that are near-twins of a registered test/sealed row (identical, or a word overlap — Jaccard — ≥ 0.6 on the source or the target side: the measure the test-score near-twin check uses), template siblings included. For a FIXED test set (teacher-written, registered — not carved by split, so split --near-dupe cannot help) whose rows mostly have a twin in training: without this, the test score measures recall of training phrases. Says how many rows it drops and what the strict subset becomes; refuses to leave nothing to train on. Also writes the twin-free model's config (--companion-config) and names the command that trains it
- `--companion-config` — with --drop-test-twins: where to write the config of the twin-free model (default: config-notwins.json beside the project's config.json) — the same config with its own run_name, data.gold and eval.near_dupe_corpus set to the --clean-to file. An existing file is never overwritten
- `--manifest` — content-free audit manifest path (default with --clean-to: &lt;clean-to>.audit.json)
- `--overwrite` — let --clean-to replace a file that is in use: one a project config trains on (data.gold, a synthetic lane, eval.near_dupe_corpus), one a run trained on, the corpus a registered split was carved from, or the output of a different audit (the all-data clean corpus vs the twin-free one). Refused without it
- `--full-indices` — --json: print every row-index list in full (by default each list longer than 5 shows its count and first 5; the audit file written beside --clean-to always keeps them in full)
- `--target-field` — 
- `--no-examples` — don't quote corpus rows in the human output
- `--show-text` — print corpus sentences even when the corpus (or the eval set a row matched) is local-only, sealed or consent-required — otherwise line numbers, ids and scores are printed instead. Only for a person at the terminal: an AI agent that reads this output sends it to its model provider. --json output never carries sentences

### `prereg new`

**Arguments:**

- `id` — 

**Options:**

- `--json` — print exactly one JSON document on stdout (other output → stderr); errors as {"error": …}, exit 2

===== SECTION: MCP server =====

# MCP Server — the agent-facing door

`champollion-mcp-server` exposes Champollion to AI agents over the [Model
Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), over stdio. It has two
profiles:

| Profile | Start it with | What it serves | Built for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **rails** (the default) | `npx -y champollion-mcp-server` | six tools: `start_project`, `project_status`, `run_next_step`, `add_data`, `try_translation`, `explain` | walking one language project from an empty folder to a measured model on the person's own computer, one step at a time |
| **full** | `npx -y champollion-mcp-server --profile full` (or `CHAMPOLLION_MCP_PROFILE=full`) | 34 tools, 3 resources and 4 prompts | discovery, benchmarking, training step by step, translating, and the network |

If you are helping someone build a translator for their language, use the
rails profile; how to drive it is in [Driving the rails over
MCP](/docs/agents/mcp), and the rules you work under are in [the operating
contract](/docs/agents/contract).

Everything here is also reachable as plain HTTP — see [Machine-readable
endpoints](#machine-readable-endpoints) — but the MCP server is the only surface
that lets an agent *act* (translate, run a benchmark, train a model) rather than
just read.

## Install

```bash
npx -y champollion-mcp-server
```

Then register it with your client. For Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add champollion -- npx -y champollion-mcp-server
```

For clients configured by file (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Antigravity), add:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "champollion": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "champollion-mcp-server"]
    }
  }
}
```

For the full profile, add `"--profile", "full"` after the package name in
`args`, or end the `claude mcp add` command with `--profile full`.

## The rails profile (the default)

The six tools walk one language project from an empty folder to a measured
model on the person's own computer. Each step says exactly which tool to call,
and every question only the person can answer (who holds a file, whether a
model may learn from it, whether its text may leave the computer, what they
expect, whether the result is good enough) is handed back to them. The tools
report counts and columns, never sentences. Every tool drives the `champollion`
command line as a separate, bounded process — the same commands a person
types. This profile is built for small agents, with short instructions.

| Tool | Arguments | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `start_project` | `folder`, `from`, `to`, `target_name?`, `source_name?`, `purpose?`, `parent_dir?`, `confirmed?` | Makes a project (`champollion new`). The first call makes nothing and returns `ask_first`: say the direction back to the person, then make the call it gives for their answer |
| `project_status` | `project_dir`, `wait_seconds?` (up to 120) | The next step, read from the files (`champollion next --json`): its mode, what to say, why, and the exact call that takes it |
| `run_next_step` | `project_dir`, `step_id`, `answers?`, `confirmed?` | Runs the step `project_status` just named. A `confirm` step needs `confirmed: true` after the person said yes; an `ask_user` step needs the person's own answers; `human_only` and `wait` steps are refused with what to do instead |
| `add_data` | `project_dir`, `path`, `into?` (`parallel`, `test` or `lexicon`), `source_col?`, `target_col?`, `sheet?`, `header?`, `usfm_source?`, `replace?` | Brings in a file where it is — a spreadsheet, a Word table, a Toolbox or LIFT dictionary, an ELAN file, or USFM scripture (`champollion data add`) — and reports counts and columns, never sentences |
| `try_translation` | `project_dir`, `text` (up to 10 lines) | Translates a few of the person's sentences with the model the project serves. For a model that learned from local-only sentences it returns the address of the model's own page, never the text |
| `explain` | `topic`: `rails`, `privacy`, `quality`, `modes`, `improve` or `off_rails` | Plain-words explanations to pass on |

## The full profile

Everything below describes the **full profile** — every tool, for discovery,
benchmarking and the network:

```bash
npx -y champollion-mcp-server --profile full
```

## Read this before you rely on it

**In the full profile, fourteen of the 34 tools work from a bare `npx` install, and `translate` works
once it has an engine. The other nineteen need Python packages the npm package
does not and cannot ship.** They do not fail silently — each returns an
actionable error naming what is missing — but you should know the shape before
you plan around it.

| Tools | Work after `npx`? | What else they need |
|---|---|---|
| `search_languages`, `get_language`, `language_overview`, `list_corpora`, `get_results`, `get_run_card`, `get_metric_reliability`, `list_contests`, `get_contest`, `get_project_info`, `list_queue`, `get_queue_item`, `estimate_cost`, `get_training_guardrails` | **Yes** — read-only, served from public endpoints | nothing |
| `translate` | **Yes**, with an engine | an API key for the engine you pick — or none, with method `local` and a model server on your own machine |
| `run_benchmark`, `get_run_status`, `preview_publish`, `publish_report` | No | the eval harness — `pipx install mt-eval-harness` |
| the fifteen `forge_*` tools | No | NMT Forge 0.2.0 or later — `python3 -m pip install nmt-forge` (add `'nmt-forge[hf]'` to train and serve). It brings the eval harness with it and finds language cards on its own; no clone needed |

No clone of the repository is needed for any of it.

## What the tools do

**Browse and cost the work.** `list_queue` and `get_queue_item` walk the open
benchmark queue — the ranked list of measurements that would most improve the
map. `estimate_cost` prices a set of runs before you spend anything.

**Look things up.** `search_languages` searches the language cards by name,
code, family or region, and tolerates misspellings. Each result also says where
the language is spoken (countries, a map point, macroarea) and its other
names — only the facts its card cites a source for, each with that source, so
languages with similar names can be told apart. A location without a source is
never shown; the line says so and links the language's Glottolog record
instead. Cards filled in from champollion.dev's published card tables (in an
npm install, every language outside the bundled core set) do not carry
per-field sources yet — they arrive with the tables' next upload — so those
lines carry the Glottolog link rather than a location. `language_overview` is the
one-page starting point for building for a language: what exists, what can
run, and the next steps. `get_language` returns the full cited card.
`list_corpora` lists the registered evaluation
corpora for a language pair or benchmark family — metadata only (size,
license, contamination grade, and whether the harness can fetch it, needs an
access token, or holds it in quarantine); corpus content is never returned,
and a pair whose corpora are all quarantined says so instead of looking
unsupported. `get_results` and `get_run_card` read scored runs off
the public leaderboard. `get_metric_reliability` answers the question most
agents get wrong — *which metric should I trust for this target language* —
from correlations with human judgments per language family. `list_contests`
and `get_contest` show contests and their declared terms; entering one is a
human-authorized CLI step, never a tool.

**Act.** `translate` runs text through the tested pipeline, with Translation
Memory (repeats cost nothing) and a deterministic quality gate. Every answer
names the engine that actually ran, with its model and endpoint where it has
them.
`run_benchmark` starts an evaluation and returns a **job id immediately**,
because real runs outlast any client timeout; you poll `get_run_status` with
that id. A job survives a restart of the server: the run keeps going, and
polling the same id afterwards still returns its status and results. Nothing
is published unless you pass `publish: true`; the plan then says what would go
public — every row with its sentence text, or scores only; the prompt, or only
its hash; and where — and a real publish needs `publish_ack` in the exact
words the plan gives, so the user has seen them first. A run made without it
can be published later, behind the same gate. `preview_publish` is read-only:
it shows the harness's own publish preview, the exact words and the exact
`publish_report` call that would publish it, and it cannot publish. It
carries the MCP annotation `readOnlyHint: true`, so an agent host that asks
before every write can allow it on its own. `publish_report` does the write
(annotated `destructiveHint` and `openWorldHint`), and `scores_only`
withholds the sentence text. Every plan also opens with the
target language's `EVAL PACK:` status — `missing` (with the command that
installs it), `ready`, or `none needed` — and names the corpus licence and its
`do_not_train` term, because the run passes `--yes`. A missing FST (the
analyzer or its pyhfst runtime) never stops the run: it proceeds, and the run
card marks FST acceptance not computed. Any other missing piece stops the run
before it translates. `skip_fst` and `skip_eval_standard` score without those
pieces, and the run card marks what was left out. The plan also says whether
COMET will be computed (the harness computes it whenever `unbabel-comet` is
installed; `comet: true` makes the run require it), and `metricx` and `fuse`
ask for the harness's opt-in MetricX-24 and FUSE-style comparator. For each
one the plan says, from the harness, whether it is installed, what to install
and what it downloads. A confirmed run that asks for a metric the harness
cannot compute is refused rather than run without it. The plan's `Results:`
and `Cache:` lines say where the run log, report and translation cache land.
A test file inside a folder that `mt-eval contest prepare` marks releasable
(a contest's `public/`) runs into the contest's `runs/` folder instead, so
nothing a run writes is released with it. A model on your own
machine (a local server, or `method: "local-model"`, which the harness runs
in-process and needs no attestation) is reported as `$0 API cost (runs on
this machine)`.

**Train without fooling yourself.** `get_training_guardrails` returns the rules
extracted from real measured failures. The fifteen `forge_*` tools run
[NMT Forge](/docs/agents/training) one guarded step
at a time — `forge_status` first and after every step (it names the next
command and the tool that runs it), `forge_preflight` to see which gates a
command will hit before it refuses, `forge_prereg_template` and `forge_prereg`
to write predictions down before any test score exists (and before any
benchmark on the test set: a scoring read blocks a later preregistration),
`forge_export` to score the test set once and package the trained model,
`forge_compare` to A/B two models with each one's near-twin caveat beside
the winner, and
`forge_prereg_verdict` to record the user's own verdict on a prediction forge
cannot judge (a free-text range) — shown as a human verdict, never as a
computed one. `forge_status` lists every trained run with its dev score and
says when a dev set is saturated (a perfect dev score with nothing for
checkpoint selection to choose between). When the eval harness puts a caveat
on a test score (for example a near-constant output: a handful of outputs
given for every source sentence), `forge_export`, `forge_status`,
`forge_compare` and `forge_lint` carry it in the harness's own words, and a
major one comes first in the next step: the score is never quoted without
it. A refusal comes back
with what went wrong, why it matters and the fix. Two steps outlive any tool
call and run in a terminal instead: training (`nmt-forge run`) and serving the
exported model (`nmt-forge serve`, which puts it behind a local endpoint that
`translate` and the CLI can use).

### Arguments

`name` is required and `name?` is optional. Every tool that takes one
language also accepts it as `language`: "`code` or `language`" means either
name works, and you pass one. The original names keep working.

| Tool | Arguments |
|---|---|
| `search_languages` | `query` or `language`, `limit?` |
| `language_overview` | `code` or `language`, `source?` |
| `get_language` | `code` or `language`, `format?` |
| `list_corpora` | `source_language?`, `target_language?`, `family?` (at least one of these three), `include_quarantined?`, `limit?` |
| `get_results` | `source_language?`, `target_language?`, `model?`, `sort?`, `limit?` |
| `get_run_card` | `id` |
| `get_metric_reliability` | `target` or `language` |
| `list_contests` | `status?`, `language?`, `limit?` |
| `get_contest` | `id` |
| `get_project_info` | none |
| `list_queue` | `language?`, `source_language?`, `model?`, `budget?`, `condition?`, `limit?` |
| `get_queue_item` | `id?` or `priority?` (one of them) |
| `estimate_cost` | `budget?`, `language?`, `source_language?`, `model?`, `condition?` |
| `get_training_guardrails` | `topic?` |
| `translate` | `texts`, `source_language`, `target_language`, `method?`, `model?`, `base_url?`, `endpoint?`, `register?`, `project_dir?`, `context?` (a gettext msgctxt: one for every text, or one per text), `script?`, `use_tm?`, `validate?` |
| `run_benchmark` | one mode: `budget?` or `top?` (queue), `item_id?`, or `corpus?` with `model?` (with `method_dir`, the model the plugin loads), `method?` or `method_dir?` (a method plugin directory; `local-model` needs `model` — it has no default), `allow_model_pair_mismatch?` (`local-model`: run an OPUS-MT pair model that names another pair, as a related-language baseline), `attest_local_transport?` (an MT engine or a plugin; never needed for `local-model`), `provider?`, `base_url?`, `target_language?`, `script?` (LLM runs: the ISO 15924 script the output must be written in, such as `Cans` or `Latn`; the plan says when the target's card lists more than one), `source_language?`, `source_field?`, `target_field?`, `max_cost?`, `coaching_file?`, `glossary?`, `attest_no_training?`, `accept_nc_terms?`, `skip_fst?` and `skip_eval_standard?` (item and corpus runs: score without the FST or the eval-standard metrics, marked not computed), `comet?` (require COMET: the run is refused while it is not installed), `metricx?` with `metricx_model?`, and `fuse?` (item and corpus runs: the harness's opt-in MetricX-24 and FUSE-style comparator, refused while not installed); then `dry_run?`, `confirm?`, `publish?`, `publish_ack?` (with a real publish: the exact words the plan prints), `anonymous?` |
| `get_run_status` | `job_id?` |

| `publish_report` | `report` (a finished run's `*_report.json`), `scores_only?`, `redact_coaching?`, `anonymous?`, `confirm?`, `publish_ack?` (the exact words the preview prints) |
| `forge_status` | `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_preflight` | `target` (the command to check), `config?`, `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_discover` | `code` or `language`, `cards_dir?`, `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_init` | `code` or `language`, `dir?`, `pair?`, `model?`, `base?`, `no_card?`, `name?`, `cards_dir?` |
| `forge_split` | `corpus`, `test`, `seed`, `out?` (default `data/split`, the path `forge_init`'s config.json reads), `dev?`, `register?` (a name prefix, or `true` for `project`), `allow_rotate?`, `near_dupe?` (a Jaccard threshold such as 0.6, when forge recommends the near-duplicate carve), `max_group?` (with `near_dupe`: the largest near-duplicate group), `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_leak_audit` | `corpus`, `strict?`, `clean_to?`, `drop_test_twins?` (with its own `clean_to`, e.g. `corpus.notwins.jsonl` — never the all-data file), `companion_config?` (with `drop_test_twins`: where the twin-free model's config goes; default `config-notwins.json`), `overwrite?` (replace a `clean_to` file that a config, a run, a split or another audit uses — refused without it), `full_indices?` (every row-number list in full; by default long lists come back as `{count, first}`), `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |

| `forge_prereg_template` | `out?`, `force?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_prereg` | `id`, `eval_set`, `predictions`, `author?`, `config_hash?` (pin it to one run), `allow_after_reads?` (only for predictions written before the set's scored reads), `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_prereg_verdict` | `id`, `prediction` (its number, or its own id), `verdict` (`held` or `missed`), `by` (who judged), `note?`, `revise?`, `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_export` | `run_manifest`, `out`, `config?`, `no_eval?`, `no_model?`, `glossary?`, `endpoint?`, `port?`, `name?`, `force?`, `prereg?`, `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_evaluate` | `run_manifest`, `config?`, `out_hyps?`, `harness_out?`, `glossary?`, `prereg?`, `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_lint` | `manifest`, `run_manifest?`, `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_report` | `manifest`, `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |
| `forge_compare` | `eval_set`, `hyps_a`, `hyps_b`, `label_a?`, `label_b?`, `run_a?`, `run_b?` (each model's run manifest: its training data is checked for near-twins), `metric?`, `target_lang?`, `config_hash?`, `prereg?`, `override_respend?`, `workspace?`, `project_dir?` |

For example, `get_metric_reliability { "language": "crk" }` and
`get_metric_reliability { "target": "crk" }` ask the same question.

### Translating with a model you deployed

`nmt-forge serve` prints two addresses for the model it serves. Point
`translate` at either one:

| Argument | Use it with | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | `method: "local"` — an OpenAI-compatible server (also `"openai"`) | `http://127.0.0.1:8378/v1` |
| `endpoint` | `method: "api"` — the champollion API contract | `http://127.0.0.1:8378/translate` |
| `model` | LLM engines only; refused for machine-translation APIs, which have none | `llama3.1` |
| `project_dir` | any method — use that project's Translation Memory | `~/my-app` |

A server on your own machine needs no key. A remote `api` endpoint reads its
key from `CHAMPOLLION_API_KEY` in the server's environment. The tool refuses
an argument it does not know, by name, instead of ignoring it, so a misspelled
argument cannot quietly send your text to a different model.

### Where the server keeps its state

Everything lives in `~/.champollion-mcp/` (set `CHAMPOLLION_MCP_HOME` to move
it):

- **`translate`'s Translation Memory** is its own file,
  `.champollion/tm.json` in that folder. It is separate from any project's
  `.champollion/tm.json`. Pass `project_dir` to use a project's file instead,
  the one `champollion sync` uses there.
- **`run_benchmark` jobs** are recorded in `jobs.json`, which keeps the
  newest 50. Each job has a folder in `jobs/` with its output and, for a
  queue item or a registered corpus, the harness's results. A run on a test
  file you hold writes its results and cache beside that file, in
  `results/` — except a file in a folder that `mt-eval contest prepare`
  marks releasable, whose run writes to the contest's `runs/` folder. Each
  such run gets its own `mcp-run-<id>/` folder there, and `get_run_status`
  prints the `mt-eval compare` command over all of them
  (`results/mcp-run-*/*_report.json`).
  Queue runs write their reports to `eval/logs/harness/queue/` under the
  server's working folder, as the harness always does.

:::note[Spending is bounded by design]
`run_benchmark` **refuses an unbounded queue run.** You must pass exactly one
bound — `budget`, `top`, or a specific `item_id`. There is no "just run the
queue" call, because an agent that misunderstands the queue could otherwise
spend without limit.
:::

## Protocol version

Transport is **stdio only** — one server process per agent.

MCP's [2026-07-28 revision](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/)
made the protocol stateless by default, retiring the `initialize` handshake and
the `Mcp-Session-Id` header. This server is unaffected in design: it uses none
of the deprecated capabilities (Roots, Sampling, Logging), never used the legacy
HTTP+SSE transport, and already follows the new guidance for cross-call state —
`run_benchmark` mints an explicit job handle that the model passes back, rather
than leaning on a transport session.

It has **not** been upgraded to the new revision, because no published
TypeScript SDK speaks it yet. See the [server
README](https://github.com/gamedaysuits/Champollion/tree/main/mcp-server) for
the full position.

# Formats

Each thing on the rails has one format: a project, a data file's terms, a
method, a chain of checks, a deployment, and the `/translate` contract between
a translation service and what calls it. Each format is **versioned** (a
document names its format and version in `$schema`; a changed shape gets a new
version number, and the older one is still read) and **validated** against the
JSON Schema below.

Every tool reads these documents natively: the `champollion` CLI, `mt-eval`,
`nmt-forge` and the MCP server give the same verdict on the same file.

- `champollion validate [folder]` checks a project's files against these
  schemas: its `champollion.project.json`, every data sidecar
  (`<file>.champollion.json`), every `method.json`, its gate chains
  (`gates/*.json`) and its deployments (`deploy/*.json`). It reads no data
  file.
- `champollion upgrade [folder]` rewrites older shapes in the current format,
  losing nothing: a sidecar written before set/1 becomes set/1, and a key set/1
  does not know moves under `x-<key>`. An invalid sidecar is left for a person
  to fix. An older `method.json` is read as method/0 and left as it is.
  `--dry` says what would change and writes nothing.

Every document refuses keys it does not know, except keys that start with
`x-`: put your own notes there.

This page is generated from the schemas themselves, so every field on it is
exactly what the tools check.

| Format | What it is |
|---|---|
| [project/1](#project1) | Champollion project (project/1) |
| [set/1](#set1) | Data set sidecar (set/1) |
| [method/1](#method1) | method/1 — one translation method, as every tool reads it |
| [gate-chain/1](#gate-chain1) | gate-chain/1 — checks between a method's output and what ships |
| [deployment/1](#deployment1) | deployment/1 — what is deployed: one method, its gates, for one pair |
| [service-api/1](#service-api1) | service-api/1 — the /translate contract |

## project/1

**Champollion project (project/1)**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/project/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/project.v1.schema.json`.

champollion.project.json — the root of a project on the rails. It holds DECISIONS only (what the project is for, its language pair, the defaults new data gets); facts about data live in each file's set/1 sidecar, events in the ledger. Written by `champollion new`; read by every tool. Unknown keys are refused; put your own notes under an `x-` key. A language, task or service project must name its pair (checked by the loader, which says so in words).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/project/1.json` | yes | Which schema this document follows. |
| `kind` | one of `language`, `task`, `service`, `app` | yes | language = build a translation method for a pair (internal dev); task = host a sealed shared task (a bounty); service = run a translation API; app = translate an app's or site's files. |
| `name` | string, not empty | yes | A human name for the project. |
| `pair` | object |  | The translation direction. Codes as the language cards name them (ISO 639-3 such as `eng`, `crk`; a private-use code such as `qaa` for a variety without one). |
| `pair.source` | string, matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$` | yes |  |
| `pair.target` | string, matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$` | yes |  |
| `pair.source_name` | string, not empty |  | The language's name as the people building this say it. Needed for a private-use code (qaa–qtz), which no language card names; otherwise read from the card. |
| `pair.target_name` | string, not empty |  | As source_name, for the target. |
| `purpose` | string |  | What the translations are for, in the community's words (e.g. 'school newsletter and classroom phrases'). Shown back to the people deciding, never sent anywhere. |
| `defaults` | object |  | What data added to this project gets when nobody says otherwise. The rails never invent an answer: `ask` makes the tools stop and ask. |
| `defaults.transmission` | one of `local-only`, `ask` |  | local-only = new files are marked so only a model on this machine may see them (the default `champollion new` writes); ask = ask for every file. |
| `defaults.training` | one of `allowed`, `not-allowed`, `ask` |  | Whether new data may be used to train a model here: allowed, not-allowed, or ask (the default). |
| `defaults.share_scores` | one of `never`, `ask` |  | Whether scores may ever be published: never, or ask (the default). Publishing is always an explicit step. |
| `created_with` | string |  | The tool and version that wrote this file (e.g. `champollion 0.6.0`). |
| `x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |

Keys not listed here are refused, except your own `x-` keys.

A **yes** in Required on a nested field (`a.b`) means: required whenever `a` is present.

## set/1

**Data set sidecar (set/1)**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/set/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/set.v1.schema.json`.

`<file>.champollion.json` beside ANY data file (TSV, JSONL, JSON, text, a word list): who holds it, what it is for, and where its text may go. One format read by every tool (mt-eval, nmt-forge, the champollion CLI, the MCP server) — the steward sidecar, given a schema. A sidecar can only make a file STRICTER: it never loosens what a corpus envelope or a registry entry says. A sidecar written before set/1 (no `$schema`) is read as set/0 — the same fields, without the new ones — and stays valid. Unknown keys are refused; put your own notes under an `x-` key.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/set/1.json` |  | Which schema this sidecar follows. Absent on a sidecar written before set/1. |
| `transmission` | `local-only` |  | local-only = only a model on this machine may ever see the text; every tool refuses to send it anywhere. The only restriction value a sidecar sets. |
| `role` | one of `train`, `dev`, `test`, `sealed`, `input`, `resource` |  | What the file is for in the project. train = may be learned from; dev = tuning and model selection; test = the protected set scores are reported on; sealed = a test set no one outside its holders sees; input = text to translate (deployment: source only, nothing to score); resource = a dictionary, glossary or grammar the methods use. |
| `kind` | one of `parallel`, `monolingual`, `lexicon`, `grammar`, `glossary` |  | What the file holds: sentence pairs, one-language text, a word list or dictionary, grammar notes, or a terminology glossary. |
| `pair` | object |  | The direction the file's columns run (source → target), in the language cards' codes. |
| `pair.source` | string, matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$` | yes |  |
| `pair.target` | string, matching `^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$` | yes |  |
| `fields` | object |  | Which column or JSON field holds which side, when the file does not use `source`/`target`. |
| `fields.source` | string, not empty |  |  |
| `fields.target` | string, not empty |  |  |
| `terms` | object |  | What the people who hold this data said about its use, recorded where every tool can read it. |
| `terms.training` | one of `allowed`, `not-allowed` |  | not-allowed = no tool may train a model on this file (enforced by nmt-forge's training mix); allowed = it may be learned from. |
| `terms.owner` | string, not empty |  | Who holds this data, in the holder's own words. |
| `terms.speakers` | string, not empty |  | Whose words the file holds — the people who said or wrote them — in the holder's own words (a family chat or an elder's notebooks hold other people's words). |
| `terms.speakers_agreed` | one of `yes`, `not-yet`, `some-said-no` |  | Whether the people whose words these are agreed to their use: yes; not-yet (not asked yet — no model may learn from it until they agree); some-said-no (no model may learn from this file — take their words out into another file first). |
| `terms.consent_record` | string, not empty |  | Path (relative to this file's folder) of the consent note that records who agreed to what, and when. |
| `id` | string, not empty |  | The registered corpus id (written by `champollion network register-corpus`); read verbatim, never re-derived. |
| `name` | string |  | The registered display name. |
| `license` | string |  | The licence the holder states (an SPDX id or a LicenseRef-\*). |
| `tier` | one of `local-only`, `private`, `sealed`, `public` |  | The registration tier `register-corpus` recorded. |
| `segment` | string |  | The corpus segment, as in a JSON envelope (e.g. `held_out`). |
| `sha256` | string, matching `^[0-9a-f]{64}$` |  | SHA-256 of the data file when it was registered; a changed file no longer gets the card's id or grade. |
| `rows` | integer, ≥ 0 |  | Rows counted at registration. |
| `card` | string |  | Path (relative to this file's folder) of the corpora card registered for it. |
| `registeredAt` | string |  | When `register-corpus` registered the file (ISO 8601). |
| `derived_from` | string |  | The protected file this one was derived from (a split, a cleaned copy, a run's outputs); its marks were carried here. |
| `holders_agreed` | object |  | Who among the data's holders agreed that this file — the output of a method whose output is local-only — could be written where it is, outside its project, and when (written by `mt-eval translate --holders-agreed-by`). It loosens nothing: the file stays local-only for every tool. |
| `holders_agreed.by` | string, not empty | yes | Who agreed, as they were named. |
| `holders_agreed.date` | string, matching `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$` |  | When it was recorded (YYYY-MM-DD). |
| `written_by` | string |  | The tool command that wrote this sidecar. |

A **yes** in Required on a nested field (`a.b`) means: required whenever `a` is present.

## method/1

**method/1 — one translation method, as every tool reads it**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/method/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/method.v1.schema.json`.

A method's own description: what it is, how it runs (kind and that kind's one setting), what it translates, how it decodes, the card the leaderboard shows, and the measured evidence for it. Written as methods/&lt;id>/method.json in a project, by `nmt-forge export` into a model folder, by `mt-eval export` and `champollion serve --emit-manifest`; read by the champollion CLI, the eval harness and the MCP server natively. Before method/1 three unrelated documents were all called method.json (the CLI plugin manifest with `type`, the harness plugin manifest with `entry_point`, forge's export); the readers still accept those as method/0 with a warning. Kind-specific settings (engine, model, model_dir, dictionary, entry_point, service.endpoint) are required by the readers, with identical messages in both runtimes. Notes of your own go under x- keys.

## gate-chain/1

**gate-chain/1 — checks between a method's output and what ships**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/gate-chain/1.json` — a document in this format says so in its `$schema` field. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/gate-chain.v1.schema.json`.

An ordered list of gates the eval engine applies to every translated segment before it is scored or shipped (mt-eval run / test / translate --gates). People bring their own gates (founder, 2026-10-10): a gate of kind metric-threshold reads one per-segment value from a metric plugin — any plugin the harness loads, e.g. an FST validity check — and compares it with min and/or max. The first gate that refuses a segment decides what ships instead: drop (nothing), keep-source (the source text), flag (the output, marked) or fallback (the chain's fallback method's translation, if the gates accept it — else nothing). A segment the plugin cannot score is refused (no value). What is measured is what ships: the headline scores the gated output, the ungated score is reported beside it, and the refusal rate is a number of its own. Retrying a refused segment with the gate's reason comes later.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | `https://champollion.dev/schemas/gate-chain/1.json` | yes |  |
| `id` | string, matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$` | yes |  |
| `description` | string |  |  |
| `gates` | array of objects (at least 1) | yes |  |
| `gates[].id` | string, matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$` | yes |  |
| `gates[].kind` | `metric-threshold` | yes |  |
| `gates[].metric` | string, not empty | yes | The metric plugin's name (MetricPlugin.name). |
| `gates[].field` | string, not empty | yes | The key in the plugin's per-segment result (a number, or true/false read as 1/0). |
| `gates[].min` | number |  | Refuse a segment whose value is below this. |
| `gates[].max` | number |  | Refuse a segment whose value is above this. |
| `gates[].on_refuse` | one of `drop`, `keep-source`, `flag`, `fallback` | yes |  |
| `gates[].description` | string |  |  |
| `gates[].x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |
| `fallback` | object |  | What translates a segment a gate refuses with on_refuse fallback: a method that runs on this machine (a dictionary: lexicon; a model: local-model), so nothing leaves it. Its output is checked by the same gates; refused again, nothing ships. For serving and translating only: a command that scores (mt-eval run / test) refuses a chain that falls back, because the score would be partly this method's and partly the fallback's under one name (founder, 2026-10-11) — measure the fallback as a method of its own. |
| `fallback.method` | string, not empty | yes |  |
| `fallback.model` | string |  | The dictionary (lexicon) or model (local-model) it runs. |
| `fallback.x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |
| `x-*` | any |  | Your own notes: any key starting with `x-` is kept and never checked. |

Keys not listed here are refused, except your own `x-` keys.

A **yes** in Required on a nested field (`a.b`) means: required whenever `a` is present.

## deployment/1

**deployment/1 — what is deployed: one method, its gates, for one pair**

## service-api/1

**service-api/1 — the /translate contract**

Schema id: `https://champollion.dev/schemas/service-api/1.json`. Schema file: `shared/schemas/framework/service-api.v1.schema.json`.

The one contract between a translation service and what calls it. Servers: nmt-forge serve, mt-eval serve, or anyone's (a method of kind `service`). Client: the champollion CLI's `api` method (sync, translate, serve). POST /translate takes a translate_request and answers 200 with a translate_response (207 when some keys failed, listed under `errors`), or an error_response (400 a request it cannot take, 401 a missing or wrong token, 404 an unknown route, 413 too large, 500 the method failed — never a partial answer). GET /health answers a health document. A field a server does not use is ignored, never refused. What a service writes can carry what it learned from: a server whose health says output_local_only true puts output_local_only true in the meta of every translate_response, and a client writes such output only where the data's holders agreed. Held to shared/test-fixtures/framework/service-api-vectors.json.

service-api/1 has no fields of its own: it defines the bodies the contract's requests and answers carry, each below.
